title: G1b playback arm regresses 24% on Demo 2 under every clip-hiding mechanism
description:
Found by strides-kyu.3. The shell restructure is free; CONCEALING the clip's <video> is not.

Demo 2 (portrait 4K, 59.94fps — the only test clip whose sampling is throughput-limited), playback
arm (`{"sequentialSampling":{"enabled":false}}`), 5 trials per variant, paired back-to-back against
a throwaway worktree at ab5d185, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro):

  base ab5d185 (old layout, visible)      62 [57..63]
  kyu.3 layout, wrapper left `relative`   61 [56..63]   restructure is FREE
  kyu.3 layout, `fixed` but ON SCREEN     63 [57..64]   `position:fixed` is FREE
  L0  fixed offscreen + inert             47 [46..57]   -24%   (shipped)
  L3  1x1 overflow:hidden window          47 [40..59]   -24%
  L2  -z-20 behind an opaque backdrop     39 [37..47]   -37%
  L1  opacity-0 + -z-10                   34 [33..39]   -45%

Pre-registered gate is +/-10%. Every rung of design.md D2's escalation ladder fails it, and the
ladder's ordering is INVERTED — L0 is jointly the best concealed option, descending is monotonically
worse. "Descend on failure" has nowhere to go, so this is not fixable by picking a rung.

WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT EARLIER
- G1a passes. It measures an IDLE element with no competing per-frame work; the hidden element does
  still present frames (Demo 2 116 vs visible 118). The failure is proportional, not binary: fewer
  SAMPLES once something contends for the frame budget. D8's "PRIMARY instrument … decisive in
  seconds" is necessary but not sufficient and must always be run with G1b's playback arm.
- Demo 1 (landscape 4K, 25fps) reads 47 -> 47 at every rung — 40ms/frame is enough slack to absorb
  the added per-frame cost. Any gate that measures only Demo 1 reads green through this entire
  failure. Demo 2 must be in the matrix.

BLAST RADIUS (bounded)
Default WebCodecs path untouched: Demo 1 53 -> 53, Demo 2 99 -> 99, bit-identical, `sampling.path`
asserted `'sequential'` vs `'playback'` per arm. The loss lands only where canUseSequentialDecode
returns false — WebM and webcam recordings. That is exactly the population D8's own correction
identified as the one the original G1 was blind to, and the population D1's observational guard
exists to protect.

THE ONE DIRECTION THE DATA SUPPORTS
Keep the element genuinely ON SCREEN while its own analysis is in flight, and conceal it only once
that clip reaches a terminal phase. Both "visible" controls above measure at or above baseline, so
this is the shape that works. It changes what the reader sees during analysis, which is a product
decision — kyu.3 deliberately did not make it. Note it composes with D1's presentation-scoped
looping (kyu.5): "presented" and "must stay visible because it is being sampled" would become two
reasons for the same element to be on screen.

Not yet ruled out and worth measuring before designing anything: whether a genuinely visible but
very small on-screen element (scaled down, not clipped — distinct from L3, which clips a full-size
element) keeps full throughput. If it does, it is a far cheaper answer than a visible-during-
analysis surface.

Repro: node scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs --arm 'playback={"sequentialSampling":{"enabled":false}}'
--clips demo2 --trials 5 --port <free>
close_reason:
RESOLVED by measurement — the cause is on-screen vs off-screen, not any concealment technique, and a genuinely visible element keeps FULL throughput down to at least 60 CSS px.

Demo 2, playback arm, 5 trials/arm, same session, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro), sampling.path='playback' on all 30 trials, commit bf95a1a:

  visible-full (control, 264x470 = 124,256 px painted)   61 [56..62]   —
  visible-full (repeat, 321x570 = 182,756 px)            61 [49..62]   0.0%   PASS
  tiny-120     (67.5x120 = 8,100 px)                     62 [56..63]  +1.6%   PASS
  tiny-60      (33.75x60 = 2,025 px)                     62 [56..63]  +1.6%   PASS
  L0 shipped   (offscreen + inert, 0 px on screen)       49 [48..52] -19.7%   FAIL
  L0 repeat    (end of session)                          47 [46..55] -23.0%   FAIL

NO THRESHOLD. Painted area varies 61x across the three passing arms (2,025 -> 124,256 px) with throughput flat at 61-62. The discontinuity is binary: on screen or not.

The negative control held at the end of the session (47 [46..55], matching this ticket's independently-measured 47 [46..57]) and the positive control reproduced at 61 twice at two different sizes and offsets — so the session COULD resolve the known failure, making its inability to find one in the tiny arms a real null rather than a blind instrument.

RESOLUTION: keep the analysing clip's element genuinely on screen. The navbar strip thumbnail (60-120 CSS px) can simply BE the live element while that clip's analysis is in flight, reverting to the static poster once it reaches a terminal phase. No product compromise, no visible-at-size surface needed. Folded into strides-kyu.4.

title: Fix poster review findings: decoder fan-out and webcam frame-0
description:
Code review of strides-kyu.2 (commit 70b9a8a) returned two ship-blocking findings plus two test gaps against that ticket's own stated acceptance criteria.

## MUST-FIX 1 — N concurrent detached 4K decoders (CONFIRMED)
useClipPoster.ts:41 -> posterFrame.ts:202-231. `useClipPoster` is per-ClipSlot with NO cross-clip serialization, so every clip reaching status:'ready' opens its own detached <video> with preload='auto' over its full blob, CONCURRENTLY, during sampling.

This is the exact hazard the module it borrows from serializes against by construction — extractFrames.ts:474-478: 'Sequential by construction rather than by caller convention: Demo 1 is 3840x2160 and Demo 2 is 2160x3840, so N concurrent detached decoders is not an acceptable amount of memory to hold (design R3).'

Repro: FileUpload sets `multiple` and fires onSelected once per file (FileUpload.tsx:33-35), wired straight to addClip (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:218). Pick 4 files -> 4 addClip in one tick -> 4 ClipSlots mount -> 4 queueMicrotask(load) in one flush -> 4 simultaneous deriveClipPoster, each minting a 4K decoder and seeking it, while clip 1's MoveNet/WebGL sampling loop runs against the shared detector.

kyu.2's live verification was single-clip only, so acceptance criterion 2 ('does not disturb analysis') is UNVERIFIED for the multi-clip path this feature exists to serve.

Fix direction: a module-level promise chain in posterFrame.ts, matching extractSessionEvidence's posture. Serialize by construction, not by caller convention.

## MUST-FIX 2 — every webcam clip posters at frame 0 (CONFIRMED)
posterFrame.ts:126-130. `choosePosterTimestamp` returns 0 for non-finite duration. POSTER_TIMESTAMP_FRACTION's own doc (posterFrame.ts:37-42) says zero is precisely what must be avoided: 'the first frame of a real clip is routinely a fade-in, a black leader, or the runner not yet in shot.'

MediaRecorder WebM reports duration: Infinity — already asserted in-repo at EvidenceGallery.tsx:93-94. useVideoSource.ts:53 copies video.duration verbatim into metadata.durationSec. So: choosePosterTimestamp(Infinity) -> 0 -> seekTo(video, 0) short-circuits to 'already-there' (extractFrames.ts:147), skipping even the presentation wait -> drawImage of frame 0. For a self-recorded run that is the user still walking back from the camera.

Systematic for one of the app's four input modes, and silent. **posterFrame.test.ts:123 tests this case as 'falls back to the first frame' — the test locks in the defect rather than catching it.** Fix the test's intent too.

Fix direction: when duration is unusable, still target a small fixed offset rather than 0 (the existing cap is a natural candidate), degrading gracefully if that seek cannot complete. Do not simply widen the clamp.

## SHOULD-FIX 3 — both MultiClipVideoSession release sites are untested
MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:130 and :187 are exactly what kyu.2's acceptance criterion 5 ('released on clip removal and session reset') names, and MultiClipVideoSession.test.tsx has zero references to poster or releaseClipPoster. Replace either call with a no-op and the suite stays green. useClipPoster.test.ts covers the HOOK's cleanup — a different site, and specifically the one both code comments say they deliberately do NOT rely on. So 'release does not lean on React cleanup ordering' is asserted in prose and nowhere in code. sameClipSession's new `previous.poster === next.poster` line (:67) is likewise uncovered.

## SHOULD-FIX 4 — 'derives once per source' is load-bearing and unasserted
useClipPoster.test.ts never asserts deriveClipPoster's call COUNT (only not.toHaveBeenCalled at :67). ClipSlot reports up on every render and the parent re-renders on every progress tick. It is correct today because all three effect deps are useVideoSource state set once per load — the reviewer traced and confirmed this — but a future change making `metadata` a per-render object would re-decode a 4K clip on every progress tick with no failing test.

## NOT findings — verified correct, do not 'fix' these
- The `clipIds.length > 1` guard at :130 is correct, not a leak. When false, setClipIds refuses the removal, the slot stays mounted, and useClipPoster keeps owning and re-reporting that poster; releasing there would blank a live thumbnail.
- All four release paths fire, including the decode that resolves after teardown. No leak path found.
- The detached decoder is torn down on every path; the object URL is created after both null guards so no path creates one it does not revoke.
- The non-disturbance claim holds transitively — no caller-owned element is reachable.
- sameClipSession still terminates.
- The purity boundary is genuine, not nominal.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Poster derivation is serialized across clips BY CONSTRUCTION, not by caller convention
- [ ] Multi-clip poster path live-verified: 3+ clips added in one file-picker interaction, sampling.detectedFrames still in normal range, numbers recorded
- [ ] A clip with unusable duration (MediaRecorder WebM, duration===Infinity) no longer posters at frame 0
- [ ] posterFrame.test.ts:123's assertion is rewritten to express the intended behavior, not the defect
- [ ] MultiClipVideoSession.test.tsx covers release on clip removal AND on session reset — verified load-bearing by confirming the suite fails when either call is stubbed out
- [ ] useClipPoster.test.ts asserts the derive call COUNT across many re-renders
- [ ] tsc -b, npm test, eslint all clean
notes:
=== ACCURACY NOTE on finding 2's severity — the fix is right, the premise was overstated ===

The review claimed every webcam clip posters at frame 0. Measured during the fix: on Chromium 151, `recorder.start()` with NO timeslice — which is exactly what `WebcamCapture.tsx:203` calls — produces a WebM reporting a FINITE duration. The Infinity case reproduces through `recorder.start(100)` (chunked), which this app does not do.

So finding 2 did NOT reproduce through the app's actual webcam path on that browser/version. It is still a real hazard: the in-repo comment at EvidenceGallery.tsx:93-94 asserts MediaRecorder WebM reports Infinity (measured at some earlier point, possibly a different engine), MediaRecorder duration reporting is a well-known long-standing cross-browser quirk, and `useVideoSource.ts:53` copies `video.duration` verbatim with no guard.

The fix is correct and costs nothing — an unusable duration now targets a 1.0s offset and falls back to frame 0 only if that seek cannot complete. But it is DEFENSIVE hardening against a case not currently observed in this app on this engine, not the repair of a live user-visible defect. Recording this so the next reader does not over-trust the finding's framing.

Finding 1 (decoder fan-out) is unaffected by this note — it was reproduced live, 3 concurrent decoders pre-fix vs 1 post-fix, in the app's real multi-file path.

title: Reconcile the poster spec with the shipped detached-decoder implementation
description:
Wave 1 ran strides-kyu.1 (spec) and strides-kyu.2 (implementation) in PARALLEL. They disagree about how a poster is captured. This is a parallelization cost, not a mistake by either agent — neither could see the other's output.

## The disagreement
`openspec/changes/navbar-clip-shell/specs/video-input/spec.md` 'Poster frame for a loaded clip' says:
  'Deriving the poster SHALL NOT disturb the element's playback: it SHALL NOT seek, play, pause,
   mute, or otherwise write to the video element's playback state. IT CAPTURES WHATEVER FRAME THE
   ELEMENT HAS ALREADY DECODED.'
and its scenario 'A poster appears once a frame is decodable' keys on 'its element has decoded its first frame'.

The shipped implementation (commit 70b9a8a, `src/video/posterFrame.ts` + `useClipPoster.ts`) instead mints a DETACHED <video> from `videoSource.sourceBlob` with its own object URL and decoder, seeks THAT to 10% in (capped at 1s), draws, and tears all three down. `useClipPoster` reads status/sourceBlob/metadata and never `videoRef`.

## Resolution: amend the SPEC, keep the implementation
The spec's real invariant is 'never write to the canonical element's playback state'. The implementation satisfies that MORE strongly than the spec's own mechanism does — it cannot reach the canonical element at all, which is a structural guarantee rather than a discipline. The spec's literal mechanism is also worse in practice:
- The canonical element's already-decoded frame at 'ready' is frame 0, which on real clips is routinely a fade-in or black leader. A strip of black squares is worse than no strip.
- During sampling it is whatever mid-analysis frame happens to be up — non-deterministic, and different every run given this repo's documented frame-timing jitter.

The implementation was live-verified with a paired baseline arm (real GPU, code genuinely stashed for the control): sampling identical at 99/99/0 on Demo 2, Demo 1 detected 53 frames matching CLAUDE.md's documented anchor exactly, wall clock differing ~100ms in both directions. Zero measurable analysis cost.

## What to change
In `navbar-clip-shell/specs/video-input/spec.md`, requirement 'Poster frame for a loaded clip':
- Permit deriving the poster from a separate, short-lived decoder built from the retained source blob, and REQUIRE that the canonical element's playback state is never written to. Keep 'SHALL NOT seek, play, pause, mute, or otherwise write' scoped to the CANONICAL element.
- Adjust the scenario 'A poster appears once a frame is decodable' so it does not mandate capturing from the canonical element.
- KEEP unchanged: no serialization of the poster itself (data URL / blob / object URL / storage); release on removal and reset; the pure sizing/aspect math rule; the null-until-available lifecycle and neutral-placeholder consumer rule.
- Note that an object URL for the transient DECODER is permitted and must be revoked — it is not a serialization of the poster.
- Re-run `openspec validate navbar-clip-shell --strict`.

Also worth adding as a scenario, since it is the stronger guarantee the implementation actually provides: poster derivation never obtains a reference to the canonical element at all.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Spec permits the detached-decoder mechanism and forbids writing to the canonical element's playback state
- [ ] The 'no serialization of the poster' rule survives verbatim in intent, with the transient decoder's object URL explicitly carved out and required to be revoked
- [ ] Release-on-removal/reset and the pure-math rule survive
- [ ] `openspec validate navbar-clip-shell --strict` passes
- [ ] No src/ changes — the implementation is correct as shipped
close_reason: Spec amended to match the shipped detached-decoder implementation. video-input 'Poster frame for a loaded clip' now scopes the no-write rule to the canonical element and permits a derivation-owned transient decoder; added scenarios for 'never reaches the canonical element' and 'transient decoder torn down on every path'; carved the decoder's object URL out of the no-serialization rule while keeping the poster itself covered. design.md D5 rewritten with a revision note recording the parallel-execution cause and the paired-baseline evidence. proposal.md + tasks.md destaled; tasks 2.1-2.6 checked off. Verified choosePosterTimestamp clamps non-finite duration to 0, so D5's webcam duration===Infinity objection is handled. openspec validate --strict passes. Commit e276dd1. No src/ changes.

title: Build the pure per-metric annotation-geometry layer
description:
The core of Epic B. Turn each metric's exemplar into a canvas-free description of what to draw. No rendering in this ticket.

## The coordinate transform (video-native -> output canvas)
  outputSide = max(1, round(min(crop.side, maxOutputSidePx)))   // maxOutputSidePx default 640
  s  = outputSide / crop.side
  cx = (kp.x - crop.x) * s
  cy = (kp.y - crop.y) * s
Note s is round(min(side,640))/side, NOT 640/side — the rounding is in the numerator only, and computeCropRect returns FLOAT sides, so s is not exactly 1 even when side <= 640. No explicit point-mapping helper exists today; the forward transform is only implicit in the 9-arg drawImage at extractFrames.ts:327-337. The exact INVERSE already exists at movenet.ts:88-95 (`toVideoSpaceKeypoints`) — same algebra, opposite direction.

## toDrawOps cannot be reused as-is — three concrete reasons
`toDrawOps(frame): DrawOp[]` (skeletonGeometry.ts:121-164) emits `PointDrawOp {kind,name,x,y,opacity}` / `EdgeDrawOp {kind,from,to,x1,y1,x2,y2,opacity}`, with DETECTED_OPACITY 1 / INTERPOLATED_OPACITY 0.35 and edge opacity = min of endpoints. Reuse the MODEL, but it needs a variant because:
  1. coordinates are video-native with no transform hook (:130)
  2. it draws all 22 SKELETON_EDGES, not the exemplar's cropKeypoints subset — a kneeFlexion crop would get the whole skeleton, nearly all of it outside the crop
  3. no frame-level opacity multiplier: a ghosted pair needs base skeleton at 1.0 and ghost at EVIDENCE_GHOST_OPACITY 0.5, composed with each point's own detected/interpolated opacity

## Per-metric marks (researched from the calcs, not guessed)
- trunkLean: hip-mid -> shoulder-mid segment; VERTICAL ray up from hip-mid; ANGLE ARC at hip-mid between them. This is literally what atan2(dx,-dy) measures (trunkLean.ts:164-173). Two instants, each with its own arc.
- kneeFlexion: hip -> knee -> ankle chain; reference ray = hip->knee extended past the knee; ANGLE ARC at the KNEE vertex. CAUTION: the reported number is 180 - interiorAngle, so the drawn arc is the SUPPLEMENT of the value. Label accordingly. The ghost (extension trough) is legibility context only and carries no measured value (kneeFlexion.ts:69-81) — must not be captioned as measured.
- overstriding: ankle <-> hip-mid; VERTICAL plumb line at hipMid.x; HORIZONTAL caliper plumb->ankle. Not an angle.
- footStrikePattern: knee -> ankle shank; VERTICAL plumb at the knee; HORIZONTAL caliper knee.x->ankle.x, plus the +/-0.05*torso midfoot band as guide lines. Do NOT draw a shank-vs-vertical arc labelled with the value — the quantity is a horizontal offset, not an angle. ONE instant.
- stepWidth / stepWidthCm: ankle + both hips; VERTICAL midline at hipMidX, PER FRAME (a ghosted pair has TWO midlines, not one); HORIZONTAL caliper midline->ankle per instant. For stepWidth the left_hip->right_hip segment IS the normalizer and is drawable in-frame.
- armSwingSymmetry: shoulder -> elbow -> wrist, one side; HORIZONTAL line through the shoulder in each frame; TWO VERTICAL BARS for wrist.y - shoulder.y. Drawing only the two wrist positions would be WRONG — the quantity is a difference of two SHOULDER-RELATIVE offsets (armSwingSymmetry.ts:117).
- bounceCycle (verticalOscillation, verticalOscillationCm, verticalRatio): midpoint marker + HORIZONTAL line at each instant's midpoint-y. See the honesty rule below before adding a caliper label.
- verticalRatio stridePair: hip-mid marker; VERTICAL tick at each hip-mid x; HORIZONTAL caliper between ticks.
- cadence: emits nothing, by design (cadence.ts:118-129, and independently METRICS_WITHOUT_EVIDENCE at evidenceFrames.ts:97).

## HONESTY RULE — the drawn quantity is usually NOT the card's number
Do not label a mark with the metric's reported value unless they are genuinely the same quantity. They usually are not:
- bounceCycle amplitude is a whole-clip least-squares spectral fit with a c+d*t+e*t^2 trend removed (bounceInstants.ts:20-30). The pixel gap between the two ghosted midpoints is NOT the reported amplitude. verticalOscillationCm is further removed still — its fit is over integrated metre deltas from one winning run.
- verticalRatio's value is a quotient across two DIFFERENT exemplars; each image shows one factor.
- armSwingSymmetry's value is a ratio BETWEEN the two images.
- Every torso/hip-width-normalized ratio (overstriding, footStrikePattern, stepWidth) divides by a CLIP-MEDIAN body scale (bodyScale.ts:41, :68) — numerator drawable, denominator not.
- trunkLean and overstriding deliberately select the EXTREME instants (exemplars.ts:44-54) while the card reports a MEDIAN, so the drawn geometry is by construction not the reported number.
Caption marks as what was measured AT THIS INSTANT. This is the same discipline that keeps the spec's ideal-posture prohibition meaningful.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A pure, canvas-free module turns an EvidenceFramePlan into annotation draw ops in output-canvas coordinates
- [ ] The transform is exercised by unit tests including a fractional crop.side (s != 1)
- [ ] Joint layer reuses the skeletonGeometry DrawOp model and preserves detected-vs-interpolated opacity, composed with the base/ghost multiplier
- [ ] Only the exemplar's own keypoints are drawn, not all 22 skeleton edges
- [ ] Per-metric marks match the table above; kneeFlexion's supplement relationship is handled explicitly
- [ ] No mark is labelled with the card's reported value where the drawn quantity differs; metrics with no honestly drawable mark get joints only
- [ ] Zero canvas/DOM references in this module (it must run in jsdom)
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean
notes:
=== CORRECTIONS from the strides-ac9.1 spec pass (source-verified) — these override the description ===

1. **stepWidth's normalizer is HIP WIDTH, not torso length — and this row is the most dangerous, not the safest.**
   The description's per-metric table calls stepWidth safe on the grounds that 'the left_hip->right_hip segment IS the normalizer and is drawable in-frame'. That is WRONG. stepWidth divides by `estimateHipWidth`'s CLIP-MEDIAN `hipWidthPx` (stepWidth.ts:224, bodyScale.ts:56-68 — deliberately a separate function from estimateBodyScale per bodyScale.ts:46-55).
   The hip segment visible in the picture is THAT FRAME'S hip width. The value used the CLIP MEDIAN. So a reader who measures the drawn segment and divides gets a different number than the card shows — a drawable-LOOKING denominator that is not the one used. Draw the segment, but do NOT label the quotient.

2. **trunkLean's sign flips with direction of travel.** trunkLean.ts:171-173 multiplies by travelDirection. On a right-to-left runner the sign of the tilt visible on screen is the OPPOSITE of the sign the card reports. An arc labelled with the card's value would point the wrong way — not merely be imprecise. This is now a spec scenario in the inline-annotated-evidence change.

3. armSwingSymmetry's reported value is computed at armSwingSymmetry.ts:271, not :117. (:117 is the per-side half-swing excursion, which is the drawable part.)

4. stepWidthCm has NO clip-median denominator — it divides by per-frame `frame.pixelsPerMeter` (stepWidthCm.ts:248). Still not drawable (a MediaPipe world-landmark calibration is not a visible length), so same no-label rule, different reason.

Read `openspec/changes/inline-annotated-evidence/design.md` D2 for the verified per-metric table — prefer it over the description's table where they disagree.
=== DECISION YOU MUST MAKE — grafted metrics resolve annotation off the WRONG detector's frames ===
From the strides-ac9.6 code review. CONFIRMED mechanism, not yet user-visible, and it lands squarely in this ticket.

`resolveOutwardSigns`'s doc claims it is 'stepWidth.ts:222-223 verbatim, not an approximation'. True for the PRIMARY-pass stepWidth. NOT true for **stepWidthCm** and **verticalOscillationCm**, which arrive by graft from the background MediaPipe scale pass.

scalePassGraft.ts:43-50 records that grafted exemplars carry the SCALE PASS's instants while 'the only frames any consumer holds are the primary pass's', and EvidenceGallery.tsx:204 duly hands planClipEvidence `input.frames = clip.analysis.robustFrames` (MoveNet) alongside the grafted heuristics. So instantPlan resolves those exemplars' joint positions AND hip polarity off a MoveNet frame snapped within tolerance — never the MediaPipe frame the metric actually measured.

Concrete failure: front-view clip, MoveNet primary, scale pass 'agreed' (so dropGraftedExemplars does not fire). stepWidthCm selects a right-foot strike where MediaPipe put right_hip 4px right of left_hip -> outwardSign +1, a positive 'own side' offset. MoveNet's frame at the nearest sampled timestamp puts the hips 2px the other way — a coin flip at that separation, and near-frontal instants are exactly where step-width strikes live. The plan then carries {left:+1, right:-1}, the INVERSE of what the metric used, and your caliper labels a crossover strike as landing on its own side — contradicting the card's own crossover caveat (stepWidth.ts:273-277) in the same viewport.

Live-reachable: this repo's measurements record verticalOscillationCm planning an exemplar post-graft on all three test clips.

Not introduced by ac9.6 — it widened a documented, accepted seam that previously carried only a coarse crop box, where a few pixels are invisible. ac9.6 is the first to push a POLARITY through it.

DECIDE, and record the decision: (a) draw no signed/oriented mark for grafted metrics, (b) draw joints only for them, or (c) accept it with a stated argument for why the divergence cannot flip a sign in practice. Do NOT let this be discovered at draw time. Whichever you pick, correct resolveOutwardSigns' 'verbatim' doc comment to name the graft exception.
close_reason: Annotation layer shipped as src/results/evidenceAnnotations.ts. planEvidenceAnnotations(plan, maxOutputSidePx) emits flat ops carrying layer ('joint'|'measurement'), instant ('base'|'ghost'|'pair') and a composed opacity, ALL in output-canvas space via a single toEvidenceOutputSpace call site that a hygiene test pins. Dispatch is on exemplar KIND, not MetricId (bounceCycle is shared by three metrics, stepWidthStrike by two). Grafted-metric divergence resolved as option (a): polarity suppressed, geometry kept — verticalOscillationCm stays op-for-op identical to verticalOscillation, stepWidthCm's caliper draws as the unsigned span it honestly is. resolveOutwardSigns' 'verbatim' doc corrected. Ghost multiplier composes as pointOpacity x frameMultiplier, all four combinations asserted. No numeric labels anywhere, per the honesty requirement. Two deviations from the ticket, both recorded in design D12: the midfoot band is DROPPED (its half-width is a clip-median torso length and a band around the knee reads as a target zone, which this change's own spec forbids), and no caliper is emitted without a per-instant side (filed as a follow-up rather than inferred from cropKeypoints array order). 78 files / 1118 tests, tsc + eslint + openspec --strict green, nothing under src/heuristics/ touched.

title: Thread keypoints and measurement sign into the evidence plan
description:
Plumbing prerequisite. Nothing in Epic B can draw a joint or an oriented caliper until this lands.

## Gap 1 — the plan drops the keypoints
`EvidenceFramePlan` (evidenceFrames.ts:139-154) retains only `{metric, kind, side?, quality, label, base:{timestamp,opacity}, ghost, crop, demotedFromPair}`. No RobustPoseFrame, no keypoint positions, and `cropKeypoints` is consumed inside `planExemplarFrames` (:404-429) and then DROPPED.

`robustFrames` is also not threaded into the extractor at all: `ClipEvidenceInput = { sourceBlob, plan }` (extractFrames.ts:121-124), and EvidenceGallery has `input.frames` in scope (:57, :92) but passes only `{sourceBlob, plan}` (:218).

Three viable seams. PREFER THE FIRST — `planExemplarFrames` already holds both RobustPoseFrames at :401-410, so resolving there keeps everything in the pure, unit-testable half exactly as the module already does for crop rects:
  a) resolve positions (or DrawOps) into EvidenceFramePlan during planning  <-- preferred
  b) carry cropKeypoints forward and re-resolve at draw time
  c) add frames to ClipEvidenceInput and resolve in extractFrames.ts

Resolution itself is exact: `base.timestamp`/`ghost.timestamp` are the SAMPLED frame's own timestamp (evidenceFrames.ts:438-445), so `findNearestFrame` returns exactly that frame object. Note `resolvePoint` (keypoints.ts:23-30) treats 'detected' AND 'interpolated' as resolvable; only 'unrecoverable' is null — preserve that distinction, the thumbnails should show it.

## Gap 2 — the sign is missing
`travelDirection` (±1) and `outwardSign` determine the SIGN of every offset metric — overstriding.ts:177, footStrikePattern.ts:192, trunkLean.ts:171, strideLength.ts:182, stepWidth.ts:222-223. NEITHER is carried on `MetricExemplar` nor `EvidenceFramePlan`.

Consequence: a caliper or arrow claiming 'ahead of the hip' vs 'behind', or 'own side' vs 'crossed over', CANNOT be oriented from the plan today. Without this, an overstriding mark can be drawn pointing the wrong way on a right-to-left runner and nothing will catch it.

Thread whichever of these the annotation layer needs. Keep it canvas-free — jsdom has no canvas.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Both instants' keypoint positions are resolvable by the draw layer, with detected-vs-interpolated status preserved
- [ ] travelDirection and/or outwardSign are available wherever a signed mark is drawn

title: Browser reuse, not GPU non-determinism, explains much of this repo's measured run-to-run spread
description:
Unplanned finding from strides-9wp, 2026-08-29. Larger than the bead that produced it and it bears on several open tickets.

CLAUDE.md's 'Determinism caveat' attributes run-to-run variance to GPU float non-associativity and frame-timing jitter. Measured against the new fresh-process-per-trial default, a large part of it is the harness reusing one Chromium process.

Two independent 3-trial fresh-process runs on Demo 1 (6 trials total) agreed on EVERY field except elapsedMs - zero spread within a run, zero difference between runs.

The same clip under --reuse-browser spread on ~20 fields:
  segmentCount           3 <-> 4
  rejectedOtherSegment   7 <-> 10
  kneeFlexion            116.9 <-> 120.7
  verticalRatio          0.0524 <-> 0.0682  (30%)
  stepWidth              1.13 <-> 1.70      (51%)

n=2 runs per regime. A strong signal, not a proven law.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE HARNESS:
1. Several beads attribute their symptom to sampling variance and may partly or wholly dissolve under a fresh-process regime. strides-i9e is the sharpest case - it says demo1 trunkLean evidence appears in 1 of 3 runs and reasons that 'run-to-run sampling variance changes the candidate set'. Re-measure it fresh-process BEFORE doing any work on the per-side bound.
2. CLAUDE.md's determinism caveat, and the numbers-with-ranges it tells future sessions to expect, are now partly wrong. Every '[a..b]' range in that file measured under browser reuse is suspect as an overstatement of real variance.
3. Historical A/B results in this repo were measured under the reused regime. Their range columns are inflated; a null result whose arms overlapped only because of that inflation could have been a real effect.

DO NOT rewrite the historical numbers - they were honestly measured under a regime that is now documented. Add the correction, do not retrofit.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md's determinism caveat states the browser-reuse contribution with the measured evidence, and says which regime a reader should assume for the ranges recorded elsewhere in the file. strides-i9e re-measured under fresh-process before any bound change. A judgement recorded on whether any past A/B null needs revisiting.
notes:
Filed from strides-9wp's report. The fresh regime costs ~65ms per trial, so there is no tradeoff to weigh - it is strictly better and is now the default.
JUDGEMENT ON THE HISTORICAL A/Bs (2026-08-29). Every A/B recorded in CLAUDE.md predates the fresh-process default and was measured with one Chromium process across trials.

THE GENERAL PRINCIPLE, first, because it bounds how alarming this is. Within any one A/B both arms were run with the same trial structure, so the cold/warm composition is normally MATCHED across arms: regime inflation widens the range columns without necessarily biasing the arm DIFFERENCE. The exception -- and it is the only one that matters -- is an arm that INTERACTS with warmth. Anything adding per-frame wall-clock cost has its penalty amplified in the cold trial, which has the least budget. Both suspects below are exactly that shape.

1. TRACKING-CROP REVIVAL (2026-08-13) -- SUSPECT, worth re-running, highest stakes.
The ship decision (default OFF) turned on one cell: park cadence/VO confidence, off "0.63-0.69, tight" vs on "0.18-0.77, median 0.32". The on arm range spans nearly the whole interval and fully contains the off arm. Its park detectedFrames row reads 62/75/76 -- one trial 18% below the other two, the exact signature of a cold trial paying an extra per-frame cost. Tracking-crop adds real work per frame, so arm and artifact are correlated rather than independent, and the pre-registered rule that fired ("any median tier degrades -> default off") was evaluated on a median over 3 trials of mixed warmth. This is the one whose conclusion could plausibly flip. Filed as strides-2rm.

2. PERSON-OF-INTEREST COST (2026-08-15) -- SUSPECT, worth re-running, lower stakes.
The reported cost is pure throughput: track loses ~16% of detected frames, park ~25% of both. Throughput is precisely what warmth moves hardest -- measured today at +23% on multiperson (103 cold vs 127 warm) with NO code change at all. A 16-25% claimed cost sits inside the magnitude the regime alone produces. The qualitative conclusion (tiers hold, values within 2-5%) is robust and the ship decision was correctness-driven, so the default is not at risk; but the cost NUMBER should not be quoted again until re-measured. Filed as strides-2rm.

3. EAR-MID vs HIP-MID VO SIGNAL (2026-08-12) -- INSTRUMENT INVALIDATED, not worth re-running as designed.
Its dependent variable WAS cross-trial spread (hip-mid 20.5%/3.2%, ear-mid 23.8%/3.5%). Under the fresh regime cross-trial spread is zero for both arms, so the experiment has no signal left to measure -- it was measuring the regime. That does not make the null wrong, it makes it uninformative. The conclusion it supported (keep the hipMid default) is the status quo, so nothing shipped on its strength. If VO signal stability is ever revisited it needs a different design -- perturb the input, not the browser -- not a re-run. No bead filed.

4. CONCEALMENT / THROUGHPUT TABLE (2026-08-17, strides-kyu.13) -- HOLDS, no re-run needed.
The margin is wide relative to any plausible regime effect: passing arms median 61-62, failing arms 47-49, each side reproduced twice within one session, and four painted-area rungs varying 61x on the passing side with throughput flat. Its own text already documents the cold-start ramp as a distinct confound and tells the reader to run both arms before calling a low first trial a regression -- it had identified the phenomenon empirically without naming the cause. Honest caveat: the arms tails DO overlap (visible min 49, offscreen max 55), and under an all-cold fresh regime the passing arm would read nearer its own low end, narrowing the measured gap. The conclusion (never conceal the analysing video) is not at risk. No bead filed; if anyone wants a cheap confirmation this is the cheapest.

NOT AT RISK, for the record. The 4K area floor (strides / #57) was rejected on a 2.90x INTRA-CLIP squeeze against a pre-registered 4x requirement -- no range width closes a 2.90 to a 4, and both endpoints came from the same clip and scene. The VO_cm regression anchor is a fixed-value check rather than an arm comparison; it re-verifies exactly (see below).

The measurement regime of a dev-only harness is repo working knowledge, which is what CLAUDE.md is for. Filing a spec delta here would be ceremony over a documentation correction.

Note strides-09k carries one non-obvious point worth repeating here: a fresh re-run of tracking-crop is the STRICTER test, not a kinder one. Fresh-process pins every trial COLD, and cold is the condition that most penalises a per-frame cost, which is what tracking-crop adds. If the on arm still degrades a median tier under fresh trials, default OFF is confirmed on better evidence than it had.
EXTENDED MEASUREMENT (2026-08-29, main at 4173f1c, real GPU ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro asserted on every invocation, never SwiftShader; dev server on the derived per-checkout port 5216, nonce identity check green; sole GPU consumer on the machine).

title: [BUG] view.confidence is not comparable between side and front — the BSR margin saturates at ~2x the anatomical maximum
description:
`ViewDetectionResult.confidence` is not comparable between a side and a front label, because
`marginAwayFromZero(value, threshold) = clamp01((value - threshold) / threshold)` saturates at 2x
the threshold, and for BSR that point (1.10) sits at roughly twice the anatomical maximum of the
signal.

BSR = (shoulderSpread + hipSpread) / (2 * torsoLengthPx), over pose-model keypoints — shoulders
near the acromion, hips at the hip JOINT CENTRES (much narrower than external hip breadth).

    biacromial keypoint separation   ~0.33-0.41 m
    hip-joint-centre separation      ~0.16-0.22 m
    torso length (shoulder-mid to hip-mid)  ~0.47-0.52 m
      -- and measured directly in this repo: torsoMeters 0.5041 (Demo 1), ~0.47 (Demo 2), from
         the MediaPipe world-landmark scale calibration.

    dead-on front, central estimate: (0.37 + 0.18) / (2 * 0.49) = 0.561
    dead-on front, generous bound:   (0.41 + 0.22) / (2 * 0.47) = 0.670

`frontViewMinBilateralSpreadRatio` is 0.55. So the front bar sits essentially AT the signal's
anatomical ceiling, and the margin's saturation point (1.10) is about twice a value no runner can
produce. Ceiling on the front BSR margin: 0.020 central, 0.218 generous. A PERFECT front view
(SER 0, coverage 1) therefore tops out at

    ((0.020..0.218) + 1) / 2 = 0.510 .. 0.609

— structurally below the 0.7 the results view calls "High confidence".

Empirical corroboration: Demo 2 (park-approach.mp4) is a genuinely dead-on front approach and
measures BSR 0.5507, right at the central estimate — clearing the bar by 0.13% and reporting
`confidence: 0.0771`. The side direction has no such problem: `marginTowardZero(BSR, 0.30)`
reaches 1 at BSR = 0 (a true side view collapses left/right together — the synthetic fixture reads
0.04, i.e. margin 0.87), and `marginAwayFromZero(SER, 0.8)` saturates at SER 1.6, an ankle
excursion of ~0.8 m, which a running stride does reach. Demo 1 and multiperson read 0.774 and
0.753.

Live consequence beyond diagnostics: `fuseFormHeuristicsResults` (src/results/fuseHeuristics.ts)
picks the view of whichever clip reports the highest `view.confidence`. With the front branch
capped near 0.5 and the side branch routinely 0.75+, a mixed-view multi-clip session's reported
view is systematically the side clip's, whichever classification is actually better supported.

NOT a blocker for anything today: `propagate-view-confidence-to-metric-gating` (strides-ich) moved
metric gating onto `ViewDetectionResult.plausibility`, which is derived from view-vs-view
discrimination and has no saturation point, so no metric's confidence or exclusion depends on this
scalar any more. What is left is a diagnostic number that reads as if it means the same thing for
both labels, and the fusion tie-break above.

Fixing it means re-deriving the saturation point from what the signal can physically reach (or
dropping the margin formulation for the plausibility one, which already exists) — a calibration
question, deliberately kept out of strides-ich rather than folded into it. Note the related
question that survives either fix: whether `frontViewMinBilateralSpreadRatio: 0.55` should sit at
the anatomical ceiling of BSR at all, since a narrow-shouldered runner filmed dead-on may never
clear it and would be labelled `'ambiguous'` for their build.
acceptance_criteria: A front-view classification's confidence is on the same scale as a side-view one — a dead-on front clip can reach a comparable number to a dead-on side clip, rather than being capped near 0.5 by a saturation point no anatomy reaches. Demo 2's view confidence stops reading 0.0771 for a view its own geometry supports outright, and fuseFormHeuristicsResults' cross-clip view pick stops systematically preferring side clips.
notes:
Raised P2->P1 by drive 2026-08-29. This is the ROOT CAUSE of the symptom strides-ich was filed for. My 2026-08-19 review flagged demo2 reporting armSwingSymmetry at 0.977 and stepWidth at 1.000 off a view classification of confidence 0.077, and read that as a propagation failure. strides-ich showed propagation is not the defect: side is doubly ruled out on that clip (needs BSR<=0.30, got 0.5507; needs SER>=0.8, got 0.3389), so the front row is the right row and 0.977 is defensible. The 0.077 is a BROKEN MEASUREMENT of a marginal front label, and this ticket is why.

Consequence worth stating plainly: with the front BSR margin capped at 0.020-0.218, a PERFECT front view (SER 0, coverage 1) caps at 0.510-0.609 confidence — structurally below the 0.7 HIGH_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD. title: detectFootstrikes emits trailing-leg late-stance instants, biasing overstriding and footStrikePattern directionally
description:
Surfaced while implementing strides-dy8. That ticket fixed the INTERVAL consequence (stride pairs spanning a step); this is the INSTANT consequence, which dy8 deliberately left alone and which the median does NOT neutralise.

detectFootstrikes takes per-side ankle-y maxima. A trailing leg produces a secondary ankle-y maximum during the OTHER foot's stance, and those instants are emitted as footstrikes. Ground truth on Demo 1 (frame-by-frame, shoe-meets-shadow, static camera): real contact onsets at ffmpeg t = 3.90/4.60/5.16/5.84. The app's three detected strikes map to ffmpeg 3.92 (a real onset), 4.96 (contact B's toe-off) and 5.52 (late stance inside contact C). Two of three are not contacts.

WHY THE MEDIAN DOES NOT SAVE IT — the contamination is directional, not symmetric noise:
- overstriding measures ankle.x - hipMid.x along the travel direction. At toe-off/late stance the ankle is BEHIND the hip, contributing a strongly negative value and pulling the median toward 'not overstriding'. Circumstantial support from this repo's own recorded distribution: Demo 1 n=7, median 0.2266, MAD 0.2403 — a spread as large as the median, the shape of a bimodal mixture rather than one population.
- footStrikePattern measures ankle.x - knee.x. At late stance the ankle is behind the knee, which classifies as FOREFOOT. Note both demo1 and multiperson currently report 'Forefoot strike (proxy)'.

This CORRECTS an assessment made in the 2026-08-19 metric-quality review, which reasoned that footStrikePattern was less exposed because 'a late-stance instant still classifies an on-ground foot'. True but insufficient: being on the ground does not make the shank angle representative of touchdown, and the bias has a definite sign.

Both metrics currently report at High confidence (demo1 overstriding 1.00, footStrikePattern 0.86-0.93; multiperson 0.958-1.00).

The clean fix is upstream in src/heuristics/footstrikes.ts — distinguish a contact onset from a trailing-leg secondary maximum — not per-metric. cadence.ts already abandoned this path for the same underlying reason and documents it. Written up in openspec/changes/gate-stride-pairs-on-fitted-period/design.md D9.
acceptance_criteria: detectFootstrikes' emitted instants on Demo 1 align with the measured contact onsets (ffmpeg 3.90/4.60/5.16/5.84, i.e. app 3.98/4.68/5.24/5.92) rather than toe-off/late-stance instants, within one sampled frame. overstriding's Demo 1 per-instance MAD drops substantially relative to its median (currently MAD 0.2403 vs median 0.2266). Verified live on all three clips; footStrikePattern's class label re-checked against keyframes rather than assumed.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS A PARTIAL FIX, deliberately. Verified live 2026-08-29, 3 trials x 3 clips, real GPU, full seven-change stack (verify-final), branch worktree-agent-ada5d3c8fa2b3bc8d @ 48adf2e. tsc/eslint clean, 1290 tests green.

TWO ROUNDS. Round 1 was FALSIFIED by live measurement and sent back; round 2 fixed most of it; round 3 stopped at my exit condition rather than reaching for a constant.

WHAT IS FIXED — the count and rhythm. Probe of the real detected instants on demo1 (temporary [footstrike-probe], added-measured-reverted):
  baseline: 4.00 L, 5.04 L, 5.60 L                                  (3, all one side, 2 of 3 not contacts)
  round 1:  3.92 R 4.04 L 4.44 R 4.92 L 5.48 R 5.60 L 5.84 R 6.08 L 6.20 R   (9 — 2.3x OVER-DETECTED)
  round 2:  3.92 R 4.92 L 5.48 R 6.08 L                             (4)
  truth:    3.98    4.68    5.24    5.92                            (4)
Same-side spacing now 1.16s / 1.56s against an expected stride of 1.316s. verticalRatio became DETERMINISTIC (0.0353937 in 3/3 trials, 0.006% spread; round 1 gave it in 2/3 with a null). overstriding's median rose on all three clips (demo1 0.129->0.172, multiperson 0.0114->0.0697, demo2 -0.0719->+0.0151). cadence, verticalOscillation, trunkLean, kneeFlexion bit-identical on all three clips.

MECHANISM: detect on ankle_S.y - ankle_opposite.y, then select by AMPLITUDE within the clip's own fitted stride window — greedy accept in descending contact-series value, each acceptance excluding everything within (2 / fittedStepHz) / (1 + STRIDE_PERIOD_TOLERANCE), which IS strides-dy8's period-gate lower band edge. So it reuses STRIDE_PERIOD_TOLERANCE for literally the statistic it was derived for and can never drop a pair dy8's gate would accept — the two rules partition the failure space. NO NEW CONSTANT; no existing threshold moved.

Corroboration worth keeping: a verticalRatio test used to assert dy8's period gate rejected exactly two run-edge artifacts at t=0.0000 and t=3.9667; the new spacing floor removes both at source. Two independently-derived rules agreeing on precisely which instants were spurious.

*** WHAT IS NOT FIXED — PHASE. The ticket's own acceptance ('align with the measured contact onsets within one sampled frame') is NOT MET. ***
Offsets: -0.06, +0.24, +0.24, +0.16s. Three of four are 4-6 frames late. Demo 1's stance durations are 0.36s and 0.44s, so those instants sit 55-67% THROUGH STANCE, not at touchdown.

PROVEN UNFIXABLE ON THIS SIGNAL, which is why it closes rather than iterating: d_S is maximal when the two ankles are furthest apart vertically, which with S planted is the CONTRALATERAL FOOT'S SWING APEX — a real gait event, not touchdown. Sweeping the fixture's apex phase, the emitted lag tracks it one for one from 1 to 11 frames (0.04-0.44s), a range WIDER THAN A WHOLE STANCE PHASE. No constant offset can be right for every runner. Every constant-free alternative on this signal marks a different wrong event (enumerated in design.md D15).

DISPERSION — my small-sample explanation was WRONG and the agent corrected it with arithmetic. demo1 overstriding's spread widened to 73% and footStrikePattern's to 78% (confidence rose to 1.000). That is not the fewer-instants trade: during stance the planted foot is fixed while the hip advances, so the ratio falls at ~3.7 torso lengths/second on this clip; a 0.30s within-trial phase scatter moves the ratio by of order a whole torso length, several times the entire reported range. The dispersion is a SYMPTOM OF THE PHASE RESIDUAL and should collapse if and only if the phase is fixed.

Also corrected by this work: perfect side alternation is NOT evidence of correctness. d_left = -d_right identically, so the merged list alternates by construction however wrong it is. I had read round 1's alternation as progress; it was not.

Residual pinned EXECUTABLY, not in prose: footstrikes.test.ts now parameterises the fixture's swing apex and asserts the sweep plus the fact that no single offset corrects it.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: the hip-bounce inflection detector (spectralFit already exposes the phase; vertical acceleration is -g in flight and net upward in stance, so trajectory inflections ARE the contact events). Error budget puts it 0.4-1.4 frames late against 4-6 today, with no constant. Deliberately not built on this change's momentum.

title: Pair crop-growth guard saturates on 4K and cannot see arbitrarily far-apart pairs
description:
evidencePairCropGrowth (src/results/evidenceFrames.ts:620) computes cropSide(union) / max(cropSide(base), cropSide(ghost)) with BOTH sides passed through computeCropRect, which applies the min(frameWidth, frameHeight) cap and the EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX floor. When the cap binds on the union AND on the solo crop, the ratio collapses toward 1 and carries no information about how far apart the two instants are.

EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH's own doc claims the measure is 'self-cancelling under both of computeCropRect's clamps, since a floor or a cap that binds on the pair's crop binds on the single's too.' That reasoning is inverted. When the cap binds on both, the ratio does not cancel — it annihilates the signal.

Measured by calling the repo's own exported evidencePairCropGrowth with synthetic boxes (3840x2160, cap 2160, full-body box 320x1240):
  adjacent                 growth = 1.000
  half a frame apart       growth = 1.0887
  opposite edges of frame  growth = 1.0887   <-- worst possible pair, scores 1.09 against a 2.5 threshold
  (torso-sized box 260x620, opposite edges: 2.177 — still under 2.5)
  1080p, small subject 90x300, opposite edges: 2.25
The guard cannot distinguish 'half a frame apart' from 'opposite edges'. On a 4K clip with a large subject it is structurally incapable of firing at any separation.

USER-VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE, observed live: after strides-9mb, Demo 1 trunkLean emits an exemplar pairing app t=6.16 with t=3.96. Source keyframes confirm the runner is at the far RIGHT edge at 6.16 and the far LEFT edge at 3.96, having crossed the whole frame between them. The union crop saturates at 2160 and centres on empty track, so BOTH runners fall outside it. The rendered evidence image is bare track and fence with no runner and no annotation, shipped as evidence for a 13.3 degree trunk lean. That is exactly what MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY's doc says must not happen ('better to show nothing than a picture nobody should read as evidence').

LIKELY FIX: compute growth from the pre-clamp crop sides. That preserves the dimensionless intent ('the crop the pair NEEDS divided by the crop one instant NEEDS') and needs no change to EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH. Note the doc explicitly and correctly rejects a naive 'did it hit the cap' test, which would delete every ghost on a small webcam source — pre-clamp ratio is not that test.

CALIBRATION BRACKET MUST BE RE-CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. The 2.5 threshold is bracketed by two measured images: must exceed 2.190 (multiperson kneeFlexion, legible) and must not reach 3.375 (multiperson trunkLean, gh #71's whole-frame crop). Both were measured with the CAPPED formula. Re-derive both under the new formula and confirm the bracket still holds before landing. Note 3.375 = 1080/320 exactly, i.e. that pair had its union at the cap and its solo at the MIN_SIDE floor — so it is itself a saturated measurement.
acceptance_criteria: evidencePairCropGrowth distinguishes adjacent from opposite-edge pairs on a 3840x2160 frame with a full-body crop box (currently 1.000 vs 1.0887). Demo 1 trunkLean no longer renders a runner-free evidence image. The 2.190 / 3.375 calibration bracket is re-measured under the new formula and still separates those two images. EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH, EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX and MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY unchanged. Verified live on all three clips.

Verified live 2026-08-29, 3 trials x 3 clips, real GPU, combined branch verify-9mb-492 (9mb 9fa169c + 492 4fac355, clean merge, tsc clean, 1222 tests green).

Fix: evidenceCropSideDemand(box) = max(max(w,h) * 1.6, 320) — padding and the degenerate-box floor, NO frame cap. Floor deliberately retained: dropping it would let a degenerate solo box zero the denominator, evidencePairCropGrowth would return null, and isTooFarApartPair would answer false for exactly the pair it exists to catch.

SATURATION FIXED (unit-pinned): 4K 320x1240 box — adjacent 1.000 (was 1.000), half-frame 1.807 (was 1.089), opposite-edge 3.097 (was 1.089, now REJECTED). Distinct and strictly increasing; the measure can see separation again.

- Lower anchor MEASURED LIVE: multiperson kneeFlexion cropGrowth = 2.190 exactly, unchanged from the capped formula, on all 3 trials. This was the side at risk and the agent's geometric prediction (that the cap never bound on it) is confirmed.
- Upper anchor by arithmetic: multiperson trunkLean 3.375 -> 5.815, computed from box dims recorded in evidenceFrames.test.ts (34x79, 53x131, 1163px union on 1920x1080). Moves AWAY from the threshold.

NO COLLATERAL REJECTIONS: every surviving growth reading across all three clips lands in [1.000, 2.190] — demo1 kneeFlexion 1.698-1.915, VO 1.197-1.241, VO_cm 1.135-1.144, stridePair 2.068; demo2 1.000-1.142; multiperson VO_cm 1.000. All metric values/confidences bit-identical to baseline.

title: verticalRatio's stride pair spans one step, not one stride, on Demo 1
description:
Demo 1's verticalRatio evidence image captions its pair 'One stride: consecutive left-foot strikes, ghosted together. 5.04 s and 5.60 s into the clip.' — 0.56 s apart. Frame-by-frame foot-contact measurement on the source clip (25 fps, contacts read off shoe-meets-shadow, static camera) puts ground-contact ONSETS at ffmpeg t = 3.90, 4.60, 5.16, 5.84, i.e. an alternating step interval of 0.65-0.70 s and therefore a same-foot stride of ~1.30 s. The app's own cadence, 91.2 spm (0.658 s/step), agrees with that measurement (92.7 spm) — cadence is correct here.

So the two instants strideLength.ts paired as consecutive LEFT strikes are 0.56 s apart, which is about one step. Mapping app time to source time (app = ffmpeg + 0.08, the documented edit-list offset), the app's three detected strikes land at ffmpeg 3.92 / 4.96 / 5.52: the first is a real contact onset, the other two are late-stance/toe-off instants inside two DIFFERENT contacts (B: 4.60-4.96, C: 5.16-5.60), which are opposite feet. detectFootstrikes' per-side ankle-y maxima are picking up a secondary maximum while that leg trails during the other foot's stance.

Effect: strideLengthPx is measured over ~43% of a real stride, so verticalRatio = VO_px / stride_px reads roughly 2x high. Sanity check in pixel space: VO 16.3% of torso and verticalRatio 6.8% imply stride = 2.40 torso lengths ~ 1.2 m, which at 46 strides/min is 0.92 m/s — far slower than the clip shows. Doubling the stride gives ~2.8 m and ~2.1 m/s, a plausible jog.

cadence.ts already documents this exact failure mode ('spurious prominence-confirmed ankle-y extrema (not real ground-contact events) shrink the median inter-strike interval') and stopped consuming detectFootstrikes for that reason. verticalRatio, overstriding and footStrikePattern still do. Demo 1 reports verticalRatio at High confidence (0.72-0.73), so nothing surfaces the error to the reader.

footStrikePattern looks less exposed: its two Demo 1 exemplars (app t=4.00 and 5.60) both land with the foot genuinely on the ground, so a late-stance instant still classifies an on-ground foot.
acceptance_criteria: A same-side stride pair's interval is validated against the step interval implied by the clip (or against the fitted bounce period) before it is used as verticalRatio's denominator, OR verticalRatio caveats/withholds when the two disagree. Demo 1's verticalRatio either changes to ~3-3.5% or stops reporting at High confidence.

Verified live 2026-08-29, 3 trials x 3 clips, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro), worktree branch worktree-agent-a2021780d4bd8db99 @ ceee2dc.

Anti-fitting checks recorded in design.md: across the whole literature CV range the derivation yields 10.7-15%, and Demo 1's offending pair at 0.790x needs only tol < 26.5% to reject — every value the derivation could produce gives the same outcome.

RESULT — outcome (a) of the two the ticket allowed: demo1 verticalRatio 0.0523686-0.0682283 @ confidence 0.727 ('High confidence') -> null @ confidence 0, with a caveat naming the real mechanism ('extra footstrike instants were most likely detected mid-stance'). NO COLLATERAL: every other metric value and confidence on all three clips bit-identical to baseline across 9 trials. Anchors held exactly — demo1 VO_cm 4.421467928439415, fitHz 1.52 x 60 = 91.2 == cadence 91.2, subjectAgreement 52/53; demo2 10.4866; multiperson 7.16478. cadence untouched as required.

title: Rank exemplar candidates by quality instead of scoring only the argmax
description:
GitHub #70 finding 2. buildExemplars in src/heuristics/trunkLean.ts and src/heuristics/overstriding.ts takes the raw argmax among outlier-bound survivors and THEN scores it, with no fallback to the next-most-extreme instant. Coverage therefore hinges on one frame's detection status.

Measured: on Demo 1 the most-forward surviving trunkLean instant (t=4.28s, 2.355 MADs, ramp value 0.785) has detectionFactor=0 (all four torso seed keypoints interpolated), so quality is 0x0.785=0, pairQuality's min takes the pair to zero, and the metric emits NO evidence — while 18 other instants on that clip clear 1.5 MAD. Same clip under {sequentialSampling:{enabled:false}} samples a different frame set, the argmax lands on a well-tracked frame, and trunkLean emits at quality 0.664.

Fix: rank all surviving instants by quality and take the best-scoring pair.
design: This is a BUG AGAINST THE EXISTING SPEC, not a behavior change. openspec/specs/form-heuristics/spec.md:1334 'Requirement: Exemplar instants are ranked and gated by a per-instance quality score' already mandates ranking, and its scenario 'An interpolated instant ranks below an equivalent detected one' says the detected instant 'scores higher and is preferred'. Current code prefers an interpolated argmax over 18 detected candidates — a direct contradiction. Likely needs an ADDED clarifying scenario rather than a MODIFIED requirement; confirm during implementation.
acceptance_criteria: trunkLean emits evidence on Demo 1 under the DEFAULT sampler (sequentialSampling enabled). Demo 1 evidence coverage goes from 7 images/5 sections to 8/6 (trunkLean gains an image). Demo 2 and multiperson coverage do not regress. Verified live in headless Chromium on real GPU via the LAST [evidence-coverage] console line. MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY, EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX and the 3-MAD outlier bound are UNCHANGED — the ticket rules out threshold tuning as editing a criterion to match a result.
notes: OUT OF SCOPE: #70 finding 1 (the 1.5-MAD gate being structurally unreachable for overstriding — maxDevMads 1.389 on multiperson means zero instants can clear it at any detectionFactor). That is a design change. Leave GitHub #70 open if finding 1 remains after this lands.
close_reason:
Verified live 2026-08-29, 3 trials x 3 clips, real GPU, branch worktree-agent-a542237ec30133bfe @ 9fa169c (and combined with strides-492 on verify-9mb-492).

WHAT SHIPPED: buildExemplars in trunkLean.ts and overstriding.ts no longer take the value-argmax and score it afterwards. Both now call a shared selectExtremePair in exemplars.ts that RANKS every candidate by the quality it would actually be emitted with and takes the best-scoring one either side of the metric's median. The spec contradiction is resolved — openspec/specs/form-heuristics 'Exemplar instants are ranked and gated by a per-instance quality score' and its scenario 'An interpolated instant ranks below an equivalent detected one' were being violated by the code.

Correctness argument worth keeping: pairQuality is a minimum over two independent per-side scores, so max over pairs of min(q_high, q_low) == min(max q_high, max q_low). The per-side argmax IS the argmax pair — no search needed. Median split is inclusive so an instant exactly on the median stays eligible for either end. Verified by falsification: reverting only the three source files (keeping tests) fails the two new metric tests while all 15 pre-existing trunkLean/overstriding tests still pass.

Thresholds byte-identical (MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY 0.5, OUTLIER_BOUND_MADS 3, EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX 320). All metric values/confidences bit-identical to baseline across 9 trials.

*** ITS STATED ACCEPTANCE CRITERION WAS NOT MET, AND THE CRITERION WAS WRONG. ***
The ticket asked for demo1 coverage 7 images/5 sections -> 8/6 with trunkLean gaining an image. Measured: with this fix ALONE, trunkLean did emit — an image of an EMPTY TRACK. The newly-selected pair is app t=6.16 ghosted against t=3.96; source keyframes confirm the runner is at the far RIGHT edge at 6.16 and the far LEFT edge at 3.96, having crossed the entire frame between. The union crop saturated the frame cap, centred on empty track, and both runners fell outside it.

That exposed strides-492 (the far-apart-pair guard was structurally blind on 4K, scoring the worst possible pair at 1.089 against a 2.5 threshold). With 492 also applied, demo1 trunkLean is correctly all-gated-out.

So the honest net effect today is: demo1 trunkLean is still gated out, but now for the RIGHT reason (its two extremes are 2.2s apart and cannot share a crop) instead of the wrong one (an interpolated argmax vetoing 18 well-tracked candidates). No user-visible coverage gain. The 7/5 -> 8/6 criterion was written before anyone knew the pair geometry and was unachievable by this change alone; it is NOT being marked satisfied and was NOT tuned toward.

The remaining work to actually get demo1 trunkLean a usable image is strides-2i1 (no fallback to the next-best pair when the best-scoring pair is un-croppable) — the same 'no fallback' defect this ticket fixed, one level up. This change is its prerequisite.

Out of scope as briefed and still true: gh #70 finding 1, overstriding's 1.5-MAD ramp being structurally unreachable (multiperson maxDevMads 1.389). overstriding remains all-gated-out everywhere.

title: e2e silently reuses a foreign checkout's dev server on 5173
description:
This bit every agent in this session, and it bit the orchestrator too. Each one worked around it by hand; nobody fixed the cause.

`playwright.config.ts:25` sets `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`, with `baseURL: http://localhost:5173/strides/` and `command: npm run dev -- --port 5173 --strictPort`. Locally that flag is TRUE, so if anything is already listening on 5173 Playwright silently drives THAT server instead of starting one for the checkout under test.

On this machine 5173 is routinely held by another strides worktree, so `npm run test:e2e` from a feature branch tests a DIFFERENT CHECKOUT and reports the result as if it were yours.

Both directions are harmful and both were observed:
- **False PASS** — the trap CLAUDE.md already documents for `scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs`, which is why that script REFUSES to run against a server it did not start. When the arm under test is a code change behind a flag, the foreign checkout lacks the code entirely and the run reads as a clean 'no effect'.
- **False FAIL** — observed at the end of this session: e2e reported `1 failed` on a docs-only commit. Re-run on a dedicated port with `reuseExistingServer: false`, it passed 3/3. Nothing was wrong with the branch.

Every agent this session independently rediscovered this and hand-rolled a scratch config on ports 5199/5202/5203/5211/5233/5261. That is six reinventions of the same workaround, which is the signal that it belongs in the config.

FIX DIRECTIONS, pick with judgement:
- Make it refuse rather than reuse, matching `ab-person-selection.mjs`'s posture — the strongest option, since that script already establishes the precedent and its rationale in CLAUDE.md.
- Or verify identity before reusing: have the dev server expose something checkout-specific and assert it matches, so reuse stays fast when it is genuinely the same tree.
- Or default the port off an env var so parallel worktrees do not collide, and keep reuse.

design:
EXPLORED 2026-08-19 — measured, reproduced, and a fix mechanism verified. Three findings, one of which invalidates this ticket's own stated tradeoff.

FINDING 1 — THE COST PREMISE IS WRONG. This ticket says 'a cold server start is several seconds on every local run, and that tax is why the flag exists', and warns against setting reuseExistingServer:false without measuring. Measured on this machine: vite boot to first HTTP 200 = 0.66s. First full page navigation to networkidle on a cold dep cache (node_modules/.vite deleted) = 2.01s, versus 1.90s warm — so dep pre-bundling costs ~0.11s, not seconds. TOTAL TAX OF NOT REUSING: UNDER 1 SECOND. The e2e suite is a single spec with a 120s timeout driving real pose detection. The flag is saving well under 1% of a run's wall clock while risking a wrong answer.

FINDING 2 — PLAYWRIGHT'S REUSE PROBE STRUCTURALLY CANNOT DETECT THIS, so no choice of webServer.url fixes it. Vite's SPA fallback returns HTTP 200 with index.html for ANY unmatched path — verified: /strides/this-does-not-exist-at-all returns 200. reuseExistingServer only probes for a successful response, so it gets 200 from any vite server rooted at any checkout. Status codes carry zero identity information here. Any guard MUST be content-based.

FINDING 3 — REPRODUCED, then a fix mechanism VERIFIED. Started a dev server from the e9b worktree on 5173: it served 4 occurrences of centerCropOnSubject while the main checkout has 0, and playwright's configured url returned HTTP 200, so reuseExistingServer:!CI would have reused it. Content-based identity check then tested both ways: wrote src/.identity-probe.ts carrying a unique marker into MAIN, fetched that module path through the FOREIGN server -> marker absent (0); through a MAIN-rooted server -> marker present (1). Clean discriminator. Note /@fs/<abs path> returned 404 in both directions and is NOT a usable mechanism.

- [ ] Running e2e while a foreign checkout holds the port cannot silently test that checkout
- [ ] Verified by reproducing: start a dev server from a different worktree on the configured port, run e2e, confirm it refuses or starts its own rather than reusing
- [ ] Local run cost is stated, so the tradeoff against the flag's original purpose is explicit
notes:
RECOMMENDED FIX, in light of finding 1: the tradeoff this ticket worried about does not exist, so take the strong option.

1. reuseExistingServer: false unconditionally (not just under CI). Costs <1s; removes the silent-wrong-checkout class entirely.
2. Derive the port from the checkout path (e.g. a hash of the repo root into a 5200-5399 range, overridable by env) so parallel worktrees stop colliding in the first place. This is what makes (1) cheap in practice — with distinct ports, a collision becomes rare rather than routine.
3. Keep --strictPort. With (1)+(2) an occupied port now FAILS instead of silently reusing. Worth a clear message: vite exits immediately under --strictPort, which playwright otherwise reports as a 60s webServer timeout rather than 'port busy'. scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs:290-297 already handles exactly this and its wording can be reused.

Do NOT rely on a content identity check as the primary guard if (1)+(2) are taken — it would be belt-and-braces for a case that can no longer arise. It IS the right tool for hand-written live-verification drivers, which is where this bug actually bit twice this session; those should assert a marker from the checkout under test appears in the served source before trusting a measurement.

Acceptance criterion 3 ('local run cost is stated') is now SATISFIED by finding 1 above.

title: Metric grid's container query has never fired: @container and @lg:grid-cols-2 on one element
description:
`MetricsPanel.tsx` renders the card grid as:

    <div className="@container grid gap-4 @lg:grid-cols-2 @3xl:grid-cols-3">

An element with `container-type: inline-size` establishes a query container for its DESCENDANTS and cannot query itself, so `@lg:`/`@3xl:` on that same element resolve against the nearest ANCESTOR query container — of which there is none. The card grid has therefore always been ONE column at every viewport width.

Measured (headless Chromium, real GPU, Demo 2, dev server on this checkout):

| viewport | grid width | computed gridTemplateColumns |
|---|---|---|
| 480 | 448 | `448px` (1 col) |
| 900 | 852 | `852px` (1 col) |
| 1440 | 1104 | `1104px` (1 col) |

1104px is comfortably past both `@lg` (32rem/512px) and `@3xl` (48rem/768px). The utilities themselves ARE generated — the served CSS contains `@container (width >= 32rem)` and `@container (width >= 48rem)` — they simply never match.

**Pre-existing, not a regression.** Present on `main` at the same line, introduced by `ee7a56e`.

**Fix** is one wrapper: put `@container` on a parent div and leave `grid gap-4 @lg:grid-cols-2 @3xl:grid-cols-3` on the child. `strides-ac9.2` uses exactly that two-node shape for the per-card query it added, for exactly this reason.

**Deliberately NOT fixed in ac9.2**, because it is a visible layout change with a product decision inside it, not a typo: today every card is full-width, which is why inline evidence sits BESIDE the description on a desktop — the behaviour the epic was asked for. Fixing the grid makes every desktop card ~311px wide, at which width the per-card container query correctly STACKS the thumbnail, and 'to the right of it on desktop' stops happening anywhere above a phone. Whoever fixes this should decide the column counts and the evidence layout together.

ac9.2 verified its own container query at all three densities by forcing `gridTemplateColumns` on the grid at a fixed 1440px viewport: 3 cols -> 311px card -> stacked; 2 cols -> 498px -> stacked; 1 col -> 1058px -> beside.
design: DECIDED 2026-08-29 by the user: KEEP ONE COLUMN. Today's full-width cards are the intended layout — they are why inline evidence sits beside the description rather than below it. The fix is therefore to delete the dead utilities, not to add the wrapper div that would make them fire. Remove '@container', '@lg:grid-cols-2' and '@3xl:grid-cols-3' from MetricsPanel.tsx:396, leaving 'grid gap-4'. Rendering must be byte-identical to today. Note MetricsPanel.tsx:268's '@container/card' is a DIFFERENT, working container (queried by descendants via @lg/card:) and must NOT be touched. Update the doc comment at :254-256 to state the one-column decision as intent rather than as a known defect, and check whether openspec/specs/results-view/spec.md asserts a responsive card grid anywhere.

Dead '@container @lg:grid-cols-2 @3xl:grid-cols-3' deleted from MetricsPanel.tsx:396, leaving 'grid gap-4' - the utilities never matched because a container cannot query itself. Rendering proven byte-identical against a zero-noise control (two consecutive baselines with no code change produced cmp-identical panel PNGs first): panel PNG, grid rect, all card rects and the card-container probe all identical at 480/900/1440, with exactly ONE computed property differing (container-type: inline-size -> normal, the declaration being removed) and nothing resolving against it. MetricsPanel.tsx:268's '@container/card' confirmed a DIFFERENT working container and left untouched - its child flips flex-direction column->row at 480->900 as the card's own width crosses @lg. Doc comment rewritten to state one column as intent. Also corrected a genuine spec falsehood found in the process: openspec/specs/results-view/spec.md's 'Evidence renders as annotated thumbnails inside the metric card' asserted a one/two/three-column grid; the delta rewrites it and adds 'The card grid is one column at every width'.

title: EvidenceInstantPlan carries no per-instant side, blocking two calipers
description:
Real gap in strides-ac9.6's seam, found by strides-ac9.7. Not a styling call.

Two exemplar kinds need to know WHICH instant's ankle was the measured one, and the plan cannot say:
- `overstrideRange` pair — loses its ankleOffsetCaliper
- `stepWidthStrike` pair — loses its ankleOffsetCaliper

The PAIR is the common case for both metrics, so this is the majority path, not an edge.

`MetricExemplar.side` is present only when BOTH instants share a side. stepWidth's pair is deliberately constructed from adjacent OPPOSITE-side strikes (exemplars.ts:207-224, stepWidth.ts:93-95), so it never carries one. overstriding's side is present only when both extremes happen to be the same foot (overstriding.ts:101).

ac9.7 REFUSED to infer it from cropKeypoints ordering. That was correct: the base's ankle is ordered first, but that is a private detail of two metric modules, and reading it would make 'which foot was measured' a silent function of an array order nobody tests.

FIX: resolve a per-instant side in `planExemplarFrames`, alongside the keypoint positions ac9.6 already resolves there. The information exists at that point — the metric knows which ankle it measured; it is simply dropped before the plan is built. Add it to `EvidenceInstantPlan`.

Check whether this needs a form-heuristics delta: if the side must ride on MetricExemplar rather than being derivable in the plan, `openspec/specs/form-heuristics/spec.md:1256-1262` ('An exemplar SHALL additionally carry: ...') must be MODIFIED in the same pass — design D8's named condition. Reuse the EXACT existing requirement title text.

- [ ] overstriding and stepWidth PAIR exemplars emit their ankleOffsetCaliper
- [ ] The side is resolved, never inferred from cropKeypoints array order
- [ ] form-heuristics delta filed if and only if the exemplar contract had to widen
- [ ] tsc -b, npm test, eslint clean
