title: Evidence extraction fans out to 3 concurrent detached 4K decoders
description:
Measured live during strides-kyu.11's multi-clip verification (headless Chromium, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro, 4-clip session: Demo 1 + 3 files picked in one interaction).

A driver-side probe counted detached <video> decoders — a <video> that gets `src` assigned while disconnected, which is exactly and only what posterFrame.ts:264 and extractFrames.ts:451 do. Attribution was by stack trace at the assignment.

    PEAK CONCURRENT BY OWNER: {"poster": 1, "evidence": 3}

`extractSessionEvidence` (extractFrames.ts:476-485) is sequential WITHIN one call, by construction and by design (its own doc names the 4K memory reason). But EvidenceGallery starts a NEW extraction pass whenever its input signature changes, and nothing serializes those passes against each other. CLAUDE.md already documents the re-extraction trigger: on a MoveNet-primary run the background MediaPipe scale pass grafts verticalOscillationCm after phase:'ready', which changes the signature and correctly triggers re-extraction — that is why two [evidence-coverage] lines appear per run.

With N clips, each overlapping pass holds one decoder, so overlapping passes multiply. Measured timeline (fixed poster arm):

    open #7  [evidence] @14220ms  evidence=1
    open #8  [evidence] @14221ms  evidence=2
    open #9  [evidence] @15291ms  evidence=3   <-- three 4K decoders open at once
    ...
    never-closed=3 at teardown

Also note 3 decoders were still open when the page was torn down, in both arms.

This is the same hazard strides-kyu.11 fixed for posters, one module over. The poster fix put the ordering inside deriveClipPoster (a module-level promise chain) precisely because N independent callers cannot serialize themselves; extractSessionEvidence has the same problem one level up — its own loop only orders the clips within a single call.

Not fixed under strides-kyu.11: that ticket's boundaries explicitly excluded EvidenceGallery.tsx, evidenceFrames.ts and extractFrames.ts as owned by a different epic.

Suggested direction: either a module-level chain in extractFrames.ts covering extractSessionEvidence the way posterFrame.ts:249 covers deriveClipPoster, or have EvidenceGallery abandon an in-flight pass before starting a new one (which would also fix the never-closed decoders).

Repro driver archived at scratchpad/multiclip-poster-drive.mjs.
close_reason:
Serialized inside extractClipEvidence (module-level evidenceQueue, the deriveClipPoster precedent) + EvidenceExtractionOptions.signal so a superseded/unmounted pass abandons instead of grinding. EvidenceGallery aborts on supersede and on unmount.

Live, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro), 4-clip session:
  peak concurrent evidence decoders 3 -> 1; evidence decoders opened 12 -> 5; gallery settles ~8s sooner.
Unmount mid-flight, identical interaction:
  open at unmount 3 -> 1; never-closed 6s later 3 -> 0; opened 9 -> 2.
Coverage unchanged: [evidence-coverage] last-line payload byte-identical before/after on Demo 1 (7 images/5 sections) and Demo 2 (5/4); 4-clip 11/8 both sides. Both clips still emit 2 lines - the scale-pass graft re-extraction is preserved, not suppressed.

Why the existing try/finally did not fire: it runs only when control leaves the try. A pass suspended at an await that is never resumed never leaves it. runIdRef invalidated the RESULT, never the WORK, so nothing signalled abandonment - measured directly: 3 open at unmount, still 3 six seconds later.

title: Draw the annotation layer onto the evidence canvas
description:
The impure half: take the annotation draw ops from strides-ac9.7 and render them onto the extracted evidence canvas.

## Where
`extractFrame` (extractFrames.ts:342-380) creates the canvas and calls `drawInstant` (:309-340) for base then ghost. Annotation is drawn after the photographic layers.

## KNOWN TRAP — globalAlpha leaks
`drawInstant` sets `ctx.globalAlpha = instant.opacity` (extractFrames.ts:326) and `extractFrame` NEVER RESETS IT before returning (:366-377). Any annotation drawn on that context after a ghosted pair silently inherits globalAlpha = 0.5. Reset explicitly; do not rely on the current value.

## Legibility at thumbnail size
These are small thumbnails, not 14rem gallery figures. Stroke widths, point radii and any text must be sized against the OUTPUT canvas, not assumed from SkeletonOverlay's constants (SKELETON_COLOR '#22d3ee', POINT_RADIUS_PX 6, STROKE_WIDTH_PX 3 — sized for a full-size video overlay). The annotation must survive being displayed small; verify by looking at it, not by reasoning about it.

The joint layer and the measurement layer need to be visually separable — a reader should be able to tell 'these are the detected joints' from 'this is the thing that was measured'.

## Preserve
- Canvas element stays in memory and is adopted into the DOM directly; no toDataURL, no toBlob, no download path (results-view spec L688; the deliberate absence is documented at EvidenceGallery.tsx:283-287).
- One detached decoder at a time, object URL owned and revoked (extractFrames.ts:443-486).

- [ ] globalAlpha is explicitly reset before annotation; a ghosted pair's annotation is not drawn at 0.5 by accident

title: Assess annotation misregistration from the 2-frame evidence seek offset (gh #69)
description:
This epic makes an existing latent bug newly VISIBLE, which is why it is scoped here rather than left on the GitHub backlog.

## The measured bug (GitHub #69, not hypothesised)
`sequentialSampling` defaults on, so most MP4s sample through WebCodecs where `robustFrames[].timestamp` is raw `sample.cts / sample.timescale` (src/video/mp4Demux.ts:174) with NO edit-list adjustment, while `HTMLVideoElement.currentTime` IS adjusted. The evidence extractor seeks a detached <video> to the planned timestamp, so every extracted frame lands late by the clip's own `elst media_time / mediaTimescale`. Ground-truthed by ffmpeg/PSNR argmax: +2 frames on all three test clips (0.0800s on Demo 1 at 25fps; 0.033367s on Demo 2 at 59.94fps; 0.033333s on the 60fps multiperson clip). Measures EXACTLY 0 under `{ sequentialSampling: { enabled: false } }` — so it is isolated to the WebCodecs domain, not to seeking.

## Why it matters now and did not before
Today's evidence images are unannotated photographs; a 2-frame offset is invisible. Once joints are drawn from the SAMPLED frame's keypoints onto an image that is 2 frames later, the skeleton floats off the body — 80ms on Demo 1 is ~12% of a step cycle, and a runner's limbs move a lot in 80ms. The annotation will look broken even though the numbers are right.

## Do not just pick a constant
`DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_SEEK_OFFSET_SECONDS` is 0 (extractFrames.ts:80) and #69 is explicit that the correct value is per-clip AND per-sampler: it must be exactly 0 for every WebM/webcam clip and every MP4 where `canUseSequentialDecode` says no. Any single constant is wrong on two of three test clips. #69 carries two real candidate fixes: plumb a per-clip offset using `src/video/containerTiming.ts`'s existing `elst` parser, or align the domains at the demuxer.

## Scope of THIS ticket
Decide, with measurement, whether annotation is acceptable at the current offset. If not, implement one of #69's two fixes. Measure misregistration in PIXELS on a real clip, not in frames — that is the number that decides it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Misregistration quantified in pixels on Demo 1 and Demo 2 with annotation drawn
- [ ] A decision is recorded: acceptable as-is, or fixed — with the measurement behind it
- [ ] If fixed: correct on WebCodecs MP4s AND exactly 0 on WebM/webcam clips and non-sequential-decode MP4s
- [ ] No single global constant is introduced as the fix
- [ ] GitHub #69 updated with the outcome (do not close it without the user's say-so)
notes:
OUTCOME: not acceptable at the current offset — FIXED. Commit b465d89 on
worktree-agent-a89f5215bd819d8bb (base 87e867c). Not pushed, not merged.

## The number (the deliverable)

Misregistration = || p(t + offset) - p(t) || for every joint an annotation
draws, scaled by outputSide / crop.side, i.e. output-canvas pixels. Measured on
the real plans of live runs (headless Chromium, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4
Pro), offset = each clip's own elst media_time / mediaTimescale.

Demo 1 (25 fps, offset 0.0800 s, 54 marks over 7 images / 5 sections), all 54
read at an exact sampled frame — zero interpolation, so these are not estimates:
  ALL   min 7.0  p50 64.5  p90 116.3  max 342.0  mean 74.5
  FAST  min 7.0  p50 83.9  p90 160.7  max 342.0  mean 93.0   (n=24)
  SLOW  min 32.5 p50 57.8  p90  80.4  max  84.9  mean 59.7   (n=30)
  worst joints: left_ankle p50 126.7 / max 342.0; right_ankle p50 72.5
  best joints:  left_knee p50 22.3; left_shoulder p50 36.6

Demo 2 (59.94 fps, offset 0.033367 s, 44 marks over 5 images / 4 sections):
  ALL   min 1.1  p50  7.2  p90 17.1  max 29.5  mean 10.1
  FAST  min 2.6  p50 12.9  p90 25.6  max 29.5  mean 13.9   (n=20)
  SLOW  min 1.1  p50  6.1  p90 10.1  max 16.5  mean 7.0    (n=24)

Display-independent framing (torso length from the clip's own scale
calibration): Demo 1 median = 31% of a torso, p90 = 56%, worst single mark ~78%.
Demo 2 median = 3.4% of a torso, max 13.7%.

FAST is only modestly worse than SLOW on Demo 1 because the dominant term there
is whole-body lateral translation across a static side-view frame, which moves
hips and shoulders as much as it moves limbs. Demo 2's subject approaches the
camera, so translation is small and the split is the expected 2x.

Verdict: Demo 2 alone would have been acceptable; Demo 1 is not. Confirmed
visually — pre-fix, footStrikePattern's shank line and ankle marker sit clearly
off the leg, and kneeFlexion's thigh/shin chain floats left of the runner.

## The fix

Option 1 (per-clip offset), derived inside extractFrames.ts rather than plumbed
through the gallery. New src/video/evidenceSeekOffset.ts:
resolveEvidenceSeekOffsetSeconds(blob) returns 0 unless BOTH the sequential
plane is on and canUseSequentialDecode(blob) says the WebCodecs path really ran,
AND the container carries a single unity-rate edit list with media_time > 0 — in
which case it returns -(media_time / mediaTimescale). Multi-entry, empty
(media_time < 0), dwell and non-unity-rate edit lists all decline to 0: none is
a constant shift. Cached per Blob. robustFrames[].timestamp untouched.

Option 2 (align at the demuxer) rejected, and not only on governance grounds:
elst media_time is pre-roll the presentation never shows, so a correct demuxer
fix must also drop those samples. That changes the sampled set, which changes
metric values — it is not the pure translation gh #69 assumed.

## Proof

ffmpeg/PSNR argmax over candidate media-frame indices, app canvas as reference:
  Demo 1 footStrikePattern: before delta 0 (24.97 vs 19.94 dB) -> after delta -2
    (24.03 vs 20.04 dB)
  Demo 2 stepWidth:         before delta 0 (22.00 vs 21.82 dB) -> after delta -2
    (22.56 vs 21.49 dB)
  Demo 1 under {sequentialSampling:{enabled:false}}: delta 0 (23.84 vs 19.63 dB,
    4.2 dB clear) — offset stayed exactly 0 on the <video> path.
The after-argmax is the media sample the analysis measured, so residual
misregistration is zero by construction.

Anchors unmoved to every digit (track clip): verticalOscillationCm
4.421467928439415, fit.frequencyHz x 60 = 91.2 == cadence.value 91.2, sinusoidR2
0.42451916621964814, sampleCount 57, span 2.24 s, torsoMeters 0.504143645953322,
medianPixelsPerMeter 868.0221516689736. Demo 2: 10.486597716761532 cm, cadence
181.2. [evidence-coverage] unchanged: Demo 1 7 images / 5 sections, Demo 2 5 / 4.

Cost: derivation 25.2 ms on the 25 MB 4K clip, 8.1 ms on Demo 2, 0 ms cached
(vs extraction's own ~3.5 s). Analysis wall clock 5805 ms on Demo 1, inside
D14's 5698 ms [5539..5910] band.

Gates: tsc clean, eslint clean, vitest 84 files / 1208 tests passing
(baseline 83 / 1188; +1 file, +20 tests).

FOLLOW-UP for whoever owns EvidenceGallery: the fact this module re-derives
(did the sequential sampler run) is known first-hand by useVideoAnalysis. If a
prop ever gets threaded onto ClipSession, this should read it instead of calling
canUseSequentialDecode a second time. The re-derivation is safe — both
predicates are pure functions of the blob and the environment, unchanged within
a session — but it is a second source of truth.

GitHub #69 updated, deliberately left OPEN for the user to close.
close_reason: Measured (Demo 1 median 64.4 output px = 31% of a torso; Demo 2 median 7.2 px), decided FIX, shipped as b465d89. Anchors and coverage unmoved; ffmpeg/PSNR argmax confirms delta -2 on WebCodecs MP4s and exactly 0 on the <video> path.

title: Author the openspec change for inline annotated evidence
description:
Spec-first ticket. No implementation. This one is unusually load-bearing because the epic REVERSES a standing prohibition — a downstream implementer who reads only the current spec will believe the work is forbidden.

  openspec new change "inline-annotated-evidence"
  openspec validate inline-annotated-evidence --strict

Capability: results-view.

## Deltas required

REMOVE (with Reason/Migration), then ADD under a fresh name — the behavior fully reverses, and per CLAUDE.md a MODIFIED block that no longer resembles the original is worse than a clean REMOVE+ADD:
- 'An evidence gallery renders below the results, grouped by metric' (L735). The gallery is gone; evidence lives in the card.
- 'Metric cards deep-link to their evidence, and are otherwise unchanged' (L770). No deep link. Note the second half of that requirement — a card with no evidence renders exactly as today, no placeholder, no empty frame, no layout shift — is still WANTED and must survive into the replacement requirement.

The single most important clause to get right, at L746 inside the gallery requirement:
  'The system SHALL NOT draw a skeleton, angle arc, reference line, or any other annotation over an
   extracted image, and SHALL NOT overlay any reference or ideal posture'
That sentence contains TWO prohibitions. Reverse the FIRST (annotating detected/measured geometry is now required). KEEP THE SECOND, explicitly and in the new requirement's own words: no reference posture, no ideal, no target overlay. Thumbnails show what was measured on this runner, never something to match. If the new spec silently drops the second half, the epic has quietly changed what the product claims.

KEEP AND EXTEND, do not rewrite: 'Evidence frames are planned purely, then extracted from a detached video element' (L648). Its purity rule ('the decision half SHALL be pure... no DOM, no canvas, no video element') now extends to annotation geometry.

Also spec: thumbnail sizing/placement in the card (below description on mobile, right on desktop), and that annotation is drawn only for metrics whose quantity is actually drawable on a still — see the per-metric determination in strides-ac9.2.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] openspec change 'inline-annotated-evidence' exists with proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md and spec deltas
- [ ] `openspec validate inline-annotated-evidence --strict` passes
- [ ] The reference/ideal-posture prohibition survives explicitly into the new requirement text
- [ ] The 'card without evidence is unchanged, no placeholder, no layout shift' guarantee survives
- [ ] The purity rule is extended to annotation geometry
- [ ] REMOVE blocks reuse exact existing requirement title text
- [ ] No src/ files changed by this ticket
notes:
CORRECTION to the description: the per-metric drawable-geometry determination is in strides-ac9.7, not strides-ac9.2 (ac9.2 is the card layout ticket).

## Third thing the spec must say — surfaced by research after this ticket was written

The spec must state that a mark is NOT labelled with the card's reported value unless the drawn quantity IS that value. Researched against the calcs, they usually differ:

- bounceCycle amplitude (verticalOscillation, verticalOscillationCm, verticalRatio) is a whole-clip least-squares spectral fit with a c+d*t+e*t^2 trend removed (bounceInstants.ts:20-30). The pixel gap between the two ghosted midpoints is NOT the reported amplitude.
- verticalRatio's value is a quotient across two DIFFERENT exemplars; each image shows one factor only.
- armSwingSymmetry's value is a ratio BETWEEN its two images; neither image shows it.
- overstriding, footStrikePattern, stepWidth all divide by a CLIP-MEDIAN body scale (bodyScale.ts:41, :68). Numerator drawable, denominator not.
- trunkLean and overstriding deliberately select EXTREME instants (exemplars.ts:44-54) while the card reports a MEDIAN — so the drawn geometry is by construction not the reported number.
- kneeFlexion reports 180 - interiorAngle, so a drawn interior arc is the SUPPLEMENT of the value.

This is the same discipline that makes the surviving ideal-posture prohibition meaningful: the images must not overclaim. Spec it as 'annotation depicts what was measured at the depicted instant', not 'annotation depicts the reported value'.

Also worth specing: cadence emits no evidence by design and is enforced in two independent places (cadence.ts:118-129 and METRICS_WITHOUT_EVIDENCE at evidenceFrames.ts:97).

Reference/ideal-posture prohibition survived and was strengthened. Honesty requirement added. Surfaced 2 corrections to strides-ac9.7's per-metric table.

description:
Put the clip strip in the navbar next to the 'Strides' wordmark (src/App.tsx:17-28 — today the header holds only an h1 and a tagline).

One thumbnail per clip, each showing that clip's OWN processing progress as an overlay on the thumbnail.

## The progress data already exists — do not build a new state machine
Per-clip `VideoAnalysisState` carries its own `phase` and `progress` (src/results/types.ts:39-59), one instance per clip via ClipSlot.tsx:51, already collected by the parent as `clipStates: Record<string, ClipSession>` (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:76). Read that.

Today progress is rendered GLOBALLY from the aggregate in ResultsView.tsx:97-123 ('Analyzing… 42%' / 'Processing results…' / 'Analysis complete.'). Per-clip progress has never been rendered anywhere except the 'Queued — waiting for another clip to finish analyzing…' line at ClipSlot.tsx:106-108.

Phases to represent: 'idle' | 'sampling' | 'processing' | 'ready' | 'error' (src/results/types.ts:6). A queued clip (one not currently holding the shared detector) needs a distinct visual from an actively-sampling one — only one clip holds the detector at a time (multiClipAnalysis.ts:163-172).

Accessibility: progress must be announced, not conveyed by the overlay graphic alone. Keep a `role="status"` text equivalent.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clip strip renders in the navbar beside the wordmark, one thumbnail per clip
- [ ] Each thumbnail shows that clip's own progress, sourced from its per-clip VideoAnalysisState
- [ ] Sampling / processing / ready / error / queued are visually distinguishable, and by more than color alone
- [ ] Progress is available to assistive tech as text, not graphic-only
- [ ] Strip is usable at narrow widths (overflow/scroll rather than wrapping the navbar)
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean
notes:
=== SCOPE BOUNDARY from the strides-kyu.1 spec pass ===
Only the PER-CLIP progress percentages move to the strip. The session-level 'Analysis complete.' line and the scale-pass narration ('Measuring more metrics with a second look at the clip…' etc.) STAY in ResultsView — results-view's 'The centimetre card reflects scale-pass progress' requires that line to be always-visible, and this epic never meant to touch it. Do not delete ResultsView.tsx:97-123 wholesale.
=== THE STRIP THUMBNAIL MUST BE THE LIVE ELEMENT WHILE THAT CLIP IS ANALYSING ===
This is now a correctness requirement, not a styling choice. It resolves strides-kyu.13 (P0).

Measured: concealing a clip's <video> costs ~20-24% of sampled frames on the playback path (WebM/webcam). A genuinely VISIBLE element keeps full throughput down to at least 60 CSS px on its longest side — 62 vs a visible control's 61, versus 47-49 concealed — with NO threshold across a 61x range of painted area. On screen or not is the only variable that matters.

So: while a clip's analysis is in flight, its strip entry hosts that clip's real, on-screen, painting <video>. Once it reaches a terminal phase, the entry shows the static poster (strides-kyu.2) and the element may be concealed again. Progress renders over it either way.

TWO TRAPS the measurement hit, both of which read as healthy if you check the wrong thing:
1. **The sticky header silently occludes the top of the page.** A 120px element at top-0 is mostly buried under the ~86px header — a partial concealment that measures like a failure while every class name looks right. getBoundingClientRect reads perfectly healthy in that case. VERIFY PIXELS: screenshot a crop of the video's own rect during analysis and confirm you see the runner, not header text.
2. **elementFromPoint is useless for this check.** `inert` removes the subtree from hit-testing while leaving it fully rendered, so the hit test returns whatever is behind the video even when the video is plainly visible.
Also: trial 1 of every harness invocation reads low despite the warm-up navigation — it inflates the range but not the median.

Note this composes with D1's presentation-scoped looping (strides-kyu.5): 'presented' and 'must be on screen because it is being sampled' become two independent reasons for the same element to be visible.

title: Evidence moves inline into annotated metric-card thumbnails
description:
Dissolve the standalone evidence gallery into the metric cards, and annotate each image with the
geometry the metric was actually derived from.

## Target end state
- Each metric card embeds its own image evidence inline: below the description on mobile, to the RIGHT
  of it on desktop.
- Evidence images become small thumbnails (today they are 14rem-wide gallery figures).
- Each thumbnail is ANNOTATED: the detected joints, plus the specific measurement geometry that metric
  computes (e.g. trunkLean = torso vector + vertical reference + angle arc; kneeFlexion = hip-knee-ankle
  chain + angle arc; stepWidth = lateral ankle separation caliper).
- `EvidenceGallery.tsx` is REPLACED by this, not kept alongside. Decided — do not re-litigate.

## Spec reversal — this is deliberate, not an oversight
`openspec/specs/results-view/spec.md` L746 currently states:
  "The system SHALL NOT draw a skeleton, angle arc, reference line, or any other annotation over an
   extracted image"
This epic reverses exactly that clause. IMPORTANT: reverse ONLY the ban on annotating detected/measured
geometry. The adjacent ban on overlaying a REFERENCE OR IDEAL POSTURE STAYS — thumbnails show what was
measured, never a target to match.

Also reversing: L735 "An evidence gallery renders below the results, grouped by metric" (full reversal —
prefer REMOVE with Reason/Migration + ADD under a fresh name, per CLAUDE.md), and L770 "Metric cards
deep-link to their evidence, and are otherwise unchanged" (no deep link; evidence is in the card).

KEEP AND EXTEND, do not rewrite: L648 "Evidence frames are planned purely, then extracted from a
detached video element". It already computes crops in video-native pixel space from the exemplar's
named keypoints — exactly the data the joint overlay needs.

## HARD CONSTRAINTS
1. jsdom in the unit suite has NO canvas (`getContext()` unimplemented; the repo deliberately refuses the
   `canvas` npm package — see src/test/canvasTestUtils.ts). Annotation geometry MUST live in a pure,
   canvas-free, unit-testable layer; only the final draw touches a rendering context. This mirrors the
   existing rule at results-view L655.
2. Extracted images stay in-memory for the session only — no data URL, no blob, no download, no
   persistence (results-view L688). Today the canvas ELEMENT is adopted into the DOM via
   `replaceChildren` (EvidenceGallery.tsx:296-316); `toDataURL`/`toBlob` are deliberately absent.
3. Evidence must never enter the `[analysis-diagnostics]` console payload (results-view L795) — its
   shape is a live-verification harness contract.

## Reuse, don't reinvent
`src/results/skeletonGeometry.ts` already emits pure point/edge DRAW OPS off `SKELETON_EDGES` with a
detected-vs-interpolated opacity distinction (`toDrawOps`). Reuse that model for the joint layer. Do NOT
write a second skeleton renderer. Note `SkeletonOverlay` the COMPONENT is coupled to a live `<video>`
and its media events — it cannot render against a static image; the reusable half is `toDrawOps`.

## Layout note
`MetricsPanel`'s card grid already uses CONTAINER queries (`@container`, `@lg:grid-cols-2`,
`@3xl:grid-cols-3` — MetricsPanel.tsx:288), the only container-query usage in the app. The
"below on mobile / right on desktop" split inside a card is a per-CARD container query, not a viewport
media query.

## Related (context only, do not close)
- GitHub #71 "Two evidence ghosts are unreadable" — whole-frame crops on far-apart pairs, and bystanders
  inside the 320px crop floor. Directly relevant: thumbnails are SMALLER, so crop quality matters more,
  and joint annotation makes a wrong-subject crop visible. Assess whether this epic subsumes part of it.
- GitHub #70 "extreme-role 1.5-MAD gate unreachable for overstriding" — overstriding emits no evidence on
  any clip measured, so that card gets no thumbnail regardless.
- GitHub #69 "Evidence seek lands 2 frames late on every MP4" — REAL INTERACTION: annotation drawn from
  sampled-frame keypoints onto a 2-frames-late image will be visibly misregistered. Joints will appear
  to float off the body. This epic makes an existing latent bug newly visible.
close_reason: Shipped and merged to main (4d625df). Evidence moved inline into annotated metric-card thumbnails; EvidenceGallery deleted; live-verified on 3 clips, real GPU. Forced past open children strides-ac9.10 / strides-ac9.12 — both are follow-ups discovered during the epic, not remaining epic scope, and stay open on their own.

title: Clips live in the top navbar
description:
Move clip management out of the page body and into the top navbar, next to the "Strides" wordmark.

## Target end state
- A clip strip in the navbar: one thumbnail per clip.
- A quick action in the navbar to record/upload another clip. It replaces the in-body "Add another clip" block once >=1 clip exists.
- Clicking a clip thumbnail opens a modal with that clip's video preview + the pose skeleton/wireframe overlay.
- Per-clip processing progress renders as an overlay ON that clip's navbar thumbnail — not as a separate global banner.
- Zero clips keeps a full-page picker; it collapses into the navbar quick-action once a clip exists.

## Why this is a restructure, not a re-style
Today `MultiClipVideoSession` renders every clip as a full-height `ClipSlot` stacked in a left column,
with a single GLOBAL aggregate progress line in `ResultsView`. There is no clip list UI, no tab bar, no
selector, and no per-clip label or thumbnail anywhere in the model — clips are positional only
(`ClipSession = { clipId, videoSource, analysis }`, src/results/multiClipAnalysis.ts:18-22).

## HARD CONSTRAINT — read before touching anything
Sampling reads frames off a live, PLAYING `<video>` element. Clip video elements MUST stay mounted while
analysing. Do NOT render them only when the modal is open — the modal reveals an already-mounted element.
Getting this wrong silently breaks analysis with no type or test error.

## Spec work

title: Re-run the tracking-crop and person-of-interest A/Bs under the fresh-process regime
description:
strides-b0y established that this repo run-to-run spread is mostly a cold-vs-warm Chromium-process split, not GPU non-determinism, and that a range column measured under --reuse-browser is a two-state mixture whose composition depends on trial index and clip order. Two historical A/Bs leaned on such a range hard enough to be worth re-measuring. Both live on the pose-backend override plane, hence the dependency on strides-4oj.

1. TRACKING-CROP REVIVAL (2026-08-13, CLAUDE.md Backlog). The default-OFF decision turned on one cell: park cadence/VO confidence, off "0.63-0.69, tight" vs on "0.18-0.77, median 0.32". The on arm range fully contains the off arm, and its park detectedFrames row reads 62/75/76 -- one trial 18% below the other two, the signature of a cold trial paying an extra per-frame cost. Tracking-crop adds real per-frame work, so the arm and the artifact are correlated rather than independent: the cold trial has the least wall-clock budget and therefore amplifies the arm penalty. The pre-registered rule that fired ("any median tier degrades -> default off") was evaluated on a median over 3 trials of mixed warmth. This is the one whose conclusion could plausibly flip.
Arms: {"trackingCrop":{"enabled":true}} vs {"trackingCrop":{"enabled":false}}, both demo clips, >=3 fresh trials/arm, real GPU.
IMPORTANT: fresh-process pins every trial COLD, and cold is the condition that most penalises a per-frame cost. So a fresh re-run is the STRICTER test, not a kinder one -- if the on arm still degrades a median tier, default OFF is confirmed on better evidence. Do not treat "it got worse" as a reason to prefer the reused numbers.

2. PERSON-OF-INTEREST COST (2026-08-15). The reported cost is pure throughput: track loses ~16% of detected frames (~4% of samples), park ~25% of both. Throughput is exactly what warmth moves hardest -- measured 2026-08-29 at +23% on multiperson (103 detected cold vs 127 warm) with no code change at all. A 16-25% claimed cost sits inside the magnitude the regime alone can produce. The ship decision was correctness-driven and the tiers-hold conclusion is robust, so the default is NOT under review; only the cost figure is.
Arms: {"personOfInterest":{"enabled":true}} vs {"personOfInterest":{"enabled":false}}, both demo clips, >=3 fresh trials/arm.

Record whatever comes back in CLAUDE.md as an ADDENDUM next to each existing table, stating the regime. Do not rewrite the 2026-08-13 or 2026-08-15 numbers -- they were honestly measured under a regime that is now documented.

For tracking-crop, the pre-registered "any median tier degrades -> default off" rule is re-adjudicated against the fresh numbers and the default is either confirmed or changed on that basis. For person-of-interest, the throughput cost is restated as a fresh-regime figure or the claim is withdrawn. CLAUDE.md gains an addendum by each table; neither historical table is edited.

title: [BUG] the front SER margin's yaw span is ~4x tighter than the side SER margin's
description:
Follow-up from strides-2iw / compare-view-confidence-across-labels (D8).

After that change every view-detection margin ramps from its view's decision threshold to a value the signal can physically reach, so both labels' confidence now spans a full 0..1 and reaches 1 at the ideal camera position. What is left is a SECOND-ORDER asymmetry between the two SER margins, in how fast they decay with camera yaw.

Using the projection model that change derives and validates (BSR(phi) = BSR_deadOnFront * cos phi, SER(phi) = SER_fullStride * sin phi, with BSR_deadOnFront ~ 0.5612 and SER_fullStride ~ 1.60):

  side SER margin  0.80 -> 1.60   spans phi 30 deg .. 90 deg   = 60 deg of yaw
  front SER margin 0.40 -> 0      spans phi 14.5 deg .. 0 deg  = 14.5 deg of yaw

So a front clip loses confidence about 4x faster per degree off dead-on than a side clip does. Measured on Demo 2, an 11-12 degree front view (both signals agree on the angle to within 1.2 deg): its BSR margin is 0.92 while its SER margin is 0.15, and the SER term alone is what holds view.confidence to 0.534 rather than something nearer the side clips' 0.75-0.77.

Not a re-run of strides-2iw: both endpoints here ARE reachable (0 is the exact foreshortening limit, and 0.40 is a real threshold), so the scale is correct. The question is whether the front label's admissible yaw envelope SHOULD be that much tighter than side's. There is a defensible reading either way -- a front clip 12 deg off really is proportionally closer to its own decision boundary -- which is why it was filed rather than folded in.

Fixing it means raising frontViewMaxSagittalExcursionRatio (0.40), which would genuinely widen the front label's angular envelope, since D5 shows SER is the binding constraint on the front label for any running subject. That is a classification change on a signal compare-view-confidence-across-labels had no measurement mandate to move. Needs its own derivation of what yaw the front label should admit, and a live A/B, before any number moves.

Full statement: openspec/changes/compare-view-confidence-across-labels/design.md D8.

title: Phase-correct footstrike detection needs the hip-bounce inflection signal, not the ankle difference
description:
Follow-up from strides-da8, which is closing as a partial fix. da8 got the footstrike COUNT and RHYTHM right (9 spurious instants -> 4, correct alternation, same-side spacing 1.16/1.56s against an expected 1.316s stride) but could not get the PHASE right, and proved that it cannot with the signal it uses.

WHY THE ANKLE-DIFFERENCE SIGNAL CANNOT DO PHASE. d_S = y_S - y_opposite is maximal when the two ankles are furthest apart vertically. With S planted, that instant is whenever the OTHER ankle is highest — the CONTRALATERAL FOOT'S SWING APEX. That is a real gait event but it is not touchdown.

MEASURED, by sweeping the fixture's swing-apex phase and reading the emitted lag back out — it tracks one for one:
  apex 0.55 -> 1.5 frames after touchdown -> emitted lag 1 frame
  apex 0.60 -> 3.0 -> 3
  apex 0.65 -> 4.5 -> 5
  apex 0.69 -> 5.7 -> 6     <- Demo 1's measured +0.24s at 25fps
  apex 0.75 -> 7.5 -> 11
NO CONSTANT OFFSET CAN CORRECT THIS. The range spans 0.04-0.44s, wider than a whole stance phase (Demo 1's own stances are 0.36s and 0.44s). An offset fitted to one runner is wrong for any runner who swings differently. This is a reason there is no constant, not a reason to pick a better one.

Every constant-free alternative on the same signal marks a different wrong event: argmax d' = fastest separation (early by the foot's deceleration time); zero crossing of d = ankles level = legs crossing (midstance, worse than shipped); band walk-back and ZUPT foot-speed-to-zero both need a constant, and ZUPT's plateau is only ~2.5x either side — the same factor-of-two shape this repo already rejected in derive-area-floor-from-4k-measurement.

THE DERIVABLE DIRECTION: the fitted hip-bounce PHASE, which spectralFit already exposes. Vertical acceleration is -g in flight and net upward in stance, so the trajectory's INFLECTIONS are the contact events — a quarter cycle either side of each minimum, one touchdown per bounce cycle, i.e. one per step. Sides still come from the ankles. Error budget against Demo 1's own stance durations: the model puts touchdown 0.164s before midstance where truth is 0.18s and 0.22s, i.e. 0.4 and 1.4 frames late, against 4-6 frames today. No constant anywhere.

FOUR KNOWN WEAKNESSES (da8 design.md D15.4): the bounce minimum is not exactly midstance; a single sinusoid forces stance = flight and those errors ARE the residual above; timing becomes a pure function of the hip fit, which is thinnest on the front-approach clip; and it inverts the current architecture. Deliberately not built on da8's momentum — it deserves its own proposal.

FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION recorded by da8, worth testing when this lands: if instants really sit 0.16-0.24s into stance at the clip's ~3.7 torso-lengths/second, a phase-correct overstriding on Demo 1 should read of order 0.5-0.9 HIGHER than the current 0.172. If the phase is fixed and the value does not move that far, one of the premises is wrong — most likely that the ankle keypoint is stationary through stance.
acceptance_criteria: detectFootstrikes' instants on Demo 1 land within 1-2 sampled frames of the measured onsets (app 3.98/4.68/5.24/5.92), versus 4-6 frames today. overstriding's and footStrikePattern's run-to-run spread on Demo 1 collapses from the current 73%/78%. No fitted constant introduced. Verified live on all three clips.

ACCEPTANCE, one by one:
1. 'instants within 1-2 frames of 3.98/4.68/5.24/5.92, vs 4-6 today' -- NOT MET AS STATED, AND THOSE ONSETS ARE WRONG. Keyframes put the real onsets at ffmpeg 4.00/4.66/5.32/5.98 (app 4.08/4.74/5.40/6.06), 1.5-4 frames later than recorded; the original set is spaced 0.70/0.56/0.68 where the corrected one is a uniform 0.66 against a fitted 0.658 step period. title: armSwingSymmetry exemplar pairs span far less than a half swing cycle
description:

On Demo 2 (cadence 181.2 spm, so a stride period of ~0.66s and an arm-swing half-cycle of ~0.33s), the [evidence-coverage] exemplars are:
  armSwingCycle:left   t=1.468133 / 1.368033  -> 0.100s apart
  armSwingCycle:right  t=0.617283 / 0.433767  -> 0.184s apart

title: No fallback to the next-best pair when the best-scoring exemplar pair is un-croppable
description:
strides-9mb fixed 'score vetoes one pre-chosen instant instead of ranking many' at the INSTANT level. The same defect exists one level up, at the PAIR level, and strides-9mb exposes it.

selectExtremePair (src/heuristics/exemplars.ts) returns the single best-scoring pair: the highest-quality candidate either side of the metric's median. Croppability of the PAIR is not part of that score and structurally cannot be — the heuristics layer is pure and has no frame size. The evidence layer then applies isTooFarApartPair (src/results/evidenceFrames.ts) and DROPS an un-croppable pair outright. Nothing tries the next-best pair. So one un-croppable winner gates the metric out, even when other well-scoring pairs sit close enough together to ghost cleanly.

Concretely on Demo 1 trunkLean: the ranked winner is app t=6.16 (runner at far right) ghosted against t=3.96 (runner at far left), 2.2s apart with the runner crossing the whole frame. There are 18 instants clearing 1.5 MAD on that clip, many of them close together in time, so a croppable pair almost certainly exists — it is simply never considered.

This is the ticket that would actually give Demo 1 trunkLean a USABLE image. strides-9mb got it to emit; strides-492 stops it emitting a blank one; this one gets it to emit a good one.

DESIGN TENSION TO RESOLVE, not to paper over: the ranking is pure and croppability is not. Options include (a) passing an optional pair-admissibility predicate into selectExtremePair so the caller supplies the frame-size-dependent test, (b) returning a ranked list of candidate pairs and letting the evidence layer walk it, (c) having the evidence layer re-rank from the metric's full candidate set. (b) keeps the purity boundary intact and matches how planExemplarFrames already consumes exemplars, but costs a wider MetricExemplar contract. Do not pick by convenience — the purity boundary is load-bearing (the unit suite runs where getContext('2d') is null by deliberate choice).
acceptance_criteria: Demo 1 trunkLean emits an evidence image whose crop actually contains the runner at both instants, verified by looking at the rendered PNG, not just by coverage counts. No metric loses evidence on demo2 or multiperson. MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY, EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH and EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX unchanged.

Per-side bounding guarantees six distinct alternatives for each end. demo1 trunkLean has ~59 eligible instants (~870 pairs); the cross product is never evaluated.
- Tie-break is pairQuality desc then SUMMED PER-SIDE RANK asc. (0,0) is that sum's unique minimum, so the head is provably strides-9mb's winner and no clip's current behaviour can shift. Breaking ties on widest deviation would have silently changed every clip.

NO REGRESSIONS: every metric value, confidence, view, sampling and scale-pass field bit-identical to baseline across 9 trials. multiperson kneeFlexion still reads cropGrowth 2.190 exactly (the calibration bracket's lower anchor) — structurally safe because its winner is already drawable so the walk stops at entry one. demo2 unchanged at 5 images/4 sections.

Constants byte-identical: MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY 0.5, EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH 2.5, EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX 320, EVIDENCE_CROP_PADDING_MULTIPLIER 1.6, OUTLIER_BOUND_MADS 3, MAX_EXEMPLARS_PER_METRIC 2.

APPROVED DEVIATION: it edited src/heuristics/types.ts (one optional 'alternates' field), which I had reserved for strides-ich. It flagged this rather than hiding it and argued the hunks are disjoint. I tested the claim by merging rather than trusting it — clean merge, both changes present.

title: Reported confidence does not track run-to-run value spread on non-deterministic clips
description:
Measured with scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs, single baseline arm, 3 trials per clip, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro), commit 4d625df. Several metrics report near-maximal confidence on values that move a lot between identical runs. Confidence is computed per run from that run's own fit quality / instance count, so it has no way to see the spread — but the spread is the reader's real uncertainty.

multiperson-track.mp4:
  overstriding        0.0114 [0.0114..0.0542]   confidence 0.958 [0.958..1.000]   -> 4.8x value spread, 'High confidence'
  footStrikePattern  -0.195  [-0.195..-0.146]   confidence 0.958 [0.958..1.000]   -> 33% spread, 'High confidence'
  kneeFlexion       109.1    [104.3..109.1]     confidence 0.848 [0.848..0.872]   -> 4.6 deg spread
  cadence / verticalOscillation / verticalRatio: value present in 1 of 3 trials, null in 2 (whole card appears and disappears between runs)

demo1 (track):
  verticalRatio       0.0524 [0.0524..0.0682]   confidence 0.727 [0.719..0.727]   -> 30% spread, 'High confidence'
  kneeFlexion       116.9    [116.9..120.7]     confidence 0.889 [0.864..0.889]
  overstriding        0.215  [0.215..0.227]     confidence 1.000

demo2 (park) is the counter-example and shows this is clip-dependent, not universal: every metric value is bit-identical across all 3 trials.

Root of the multiperson case is upstream sampling instability (detectedFrames 127 [103..127], segments[0].frameCount 123 [101..123], rejectedOtherSegment 47 [47..74]) rather than the metric math, but the user-facing symptom is a High-confidence number that is not reproducible.

Not proposing multi-run averaging in the product. The ask is that a metric whose supporting sample is this unstable should not present as High confidence.
design:
PM DECISION (drive, 2026-08-29) — resolving this ticket's two-way acceptance in favour of the CONFIDENCE side, and narrowing it so it does not become threshold-tuning.

Do NOT chase the upstream sampling instability. multiperson's detectedFrames 103-127 / rejectedOtherSegment 47-74 belong to the person-selection and sampling domain (epic #52 territory), are a much larger job, and are not what this ticket is about.

Do NOT invent a cross-run stability coefficient. This repo has twice recorded that inventing an uncalibrated coefficient from a 3-clip evidence base is the wrong move (cadence.ts's own doc on why there is no footstrike-agreement caveat; the area-floor measurement in CLAUDE.md). A term fitted to 3 trials x 3 clips would be exactly that.

DO use the WITHIN-RUN dispersion that is already computed. The cross-run instability has a within-run explanation that needs no new calibration data: multiperson overstriding has median 0.0542 with MAD 0.3993 — the MAD is ~7x the median, so the aggregate is not determined by its own instances, and which instances get sampled decides the answer. Demo 1 trunkLean by contrast is median 13.297 deg / MAD 3.016 (MAD ~23% of median) and is stable across runs. describeDistribution() in exemplars.ts already produces median and MAD per metric per run; the information is on hand at confidence time.

So: a metric whose instance-level dispersion is large relative to its own reported value should not present as High confidence. The exact form (a normalized-dispersion multiplier on confidence, or a caveat plus tier demotion) is the implementer's call, but it MUST be derivable from a single run and MUST NOT be fitted to the observed cross-trial spreads.

Expected outcome to verify: multiperson overstriding and demo1 verticalRatio drop below the 0.7 High threshold; demo2 (bit-identical across trials) does not lose confidence anywhere; demo1 cadence/kneeFlexion/footStrikePattern keep their current tiers.

NOTE ordering: strides-dy8 may resolve demo1 verticalRatio's 30% spread on its own by fixing the stride denominator. Re-measure after dy8 lands before assuming this ticket still needs to move that number.
acceptance_criteria: Either confidence for these metrics incorporates a stability/sample-adequacy term that demotes multiperson overstriding and demo1 verticalRatio below the 0.7 High threshold, or the instability is closed upstream so the values reproduce. Re-run scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs 3 trials and compare.
notes:
MEASUREMENT UPDATE (2026-08-29 baseline, 3 trials/clip, same harness that will verify the fix):

Half of this ticket's original cross-run evidence DID NOT REPRODUCE this session. multiperson overstriding came back 0.0113843 with ZERO range across all 3 trials (originally 0.0114-0.0542, a 4.8x spread), detectedFrames flat at 127 (originally 103-127), and evidence coverage flat at 4 images/3 sections (originally varying). multiperson cadence/verticalOscillation/verticalRatio were null in 3 of 3 trials this time vs 2 of 3 before.

The half that DID reproduce: demo1 verticalRatio 0.0523686-0.0682283, a 30% spread at confidence 0.727 ('High confidence').

CONSEQUENCE FOR VERIFICATION: do NOT try to verify this ticket by showing a cross-run spread shrink. That spread is itself not reliably reproducible session to session, so it cannot be the acceptance instrument — chasing it would mean tuning against noise, which is the exact failure mode the DESIGN field rules out.

Verify instead against the WITHIN-RUN dispersion, which is a property of a single run and is stable: a metric whose per-instance MAD is large relative to its own reported |median| must not present as High confidence. That statement is checkable in one run and does not depend on the cross-trial behaviour that just proved fickle.

Also note demo1 verticalRatio's 30% spread may be substantially or wholly attributable to strides-dy8's stride-pairing defect (which pairs on spurious footstrikes, so which pairs survive shifts run to run). RE-MEASURE demo1 verticalRatio after dy8 lands. If dy8 removes that spread, this ticket's remaining scope is smaller than filed and should be re-scoped rather than padded out.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS SUPERSEDED — NOT BUILT. Every piece of evidence this ticket was filed on has since been explained by a root cause with its own ticket, and adding the confidence term it asked for would now mask a bug we are already fixing.

The ticket asked that metrics reporting High confidence on run-to-run-unstable values be demoted. Its three evidence items, tracked to conclusion:

1. multiperson overstriding, filed as 0.0114-0.0542 (4.8x spread) at confidence 0.958-1.000.
   DID NOT REPRODUCE. The 2026-08-29 baseline (same harness that verified every ticket in this batch, 3 trials) returned 0.0113843 FLAT across all three trials, with detectedFrames flat at 127 (filed as 103-127) and evidence coverage flat at 4/3. The spread was session-specific.

2. demo1 verticalRatio, filed as 0.0524-0.0682 (30% spread) at confidence 0.727.
   GONE, twice over. strides-dy8 made the metric null (its stride denominator spanned one step, not one stride). strides-da8 then brought it back at 0.0353937 with a 0.006% spread across 3 trials — DETERMINISTIC. The instability was the stride-pairing defect, not a confidence-calibration gap.

3. The within-run dispersion framing I substituted when 1 and 2 evaporated (demo1 overstriding MAD 0.2403 vs median 0.2266).
   ROOT-CAUSED to strides-da8's phase residual, with arithmetic I did not have when I wrote the PM decision on this ticket. During stance the planted foot is fixed in the image while the hip advances, so overstriding's ratio falls at ~3.7 torso lengths/second on this clip; the 0.30s within-trial phase scatter moves the ratio by of order a whole torso length — several times the entire reported range. Dispersion is a SYMPTOM. It should collapse if and only if the phase is fixed, which is filed as the hip-bounce-inflection follow-up.

WHY NOT BUILD IT ANYWAY. A dispersion-based confidence penalty added now would (a) treat a symptom whose cause is understood and scheduled, (b) be calibrated against spreads that will change when the phase lands, and (c) put an uncalibrated coefficient into a user-visible score on a three-clip evidence base — which is exactly what this ticket's own DESIGN field, cadence.ts's doc on the absent footstrike-agreement caveat, and derive-area-floor-from-4k-measurement all independently rejected.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND IS TRACKED ELSEWHERE: demo1 overstriding (73% spread) and footStrikePattern (78% spread) currently report High confidence. That is real and user-visible. It is the acceptance criterion of the hip-bounce-inflection follow-up, which requires exactly that those spreads collapse — so the concern is not dropped, it is attached to its cause.

REOPEN THIS if the phase fix lands and High-confidence metrics remain run-to-run unstable. At that point the dispersion would be irreducible rather than a symptom, and a confidence term would be the right answer with real evidence behind it.

title: view.confidence is discarded, so a 0.077-confidence view classification silently gates 8 metrics
description:
computeFormHeuristics (src/heuristics/index.ts:37-51) calls detectView(frames, config) and then passes only view.view — the LABEL — to all eleven metrics. view.confidence is stored on the result for diagnostics and never read by any metric.

Measured live on Demo 2 (park-approach.mp4, 3 trials, real GPU): view.view = 'front' at view.confidence = 0.0771 (bilateralSpreadRatio 0.551, sagittalExcursionRatio 0.339, frameCoverage 1). On the strength of that 7.7%-confidence classification the panel:
  - hard-EXCLUDES six metrics as 'not reliable from a front view' (verticalRatio, trunkLean, overstriding, kneeFlexion, footStrikePattern, stepWidthCm) via viewFit 'unsuitable', which metricTier treats as structurally unmeasurable and renders with no value at all;
  - reports armSwingSymmetry at confidence 0.977 and stepWidth at 1.000 — 'High confidence' cards — because those are viewFit 'primary' for 'front'.

Both directions are wrong at that view confidence. An exclusion asserts the camera geometry cannot support the measurement; a 0.977 confidence asserts it definitely can. Neither claim is supportable from a classification the detector itself is 7.7% sure of.

Compare Demo 1 (side, 0.76) and multiperson (side, 0.75), where the same machinery is on much firmer ground. The gap is only visible in [analysis-diagnostics]; nothing in the UI reflects it.

Note viewDetection.ts already has the vocabulary for this — its own doc says an honest 'ambiguous' just degrades confidence, and it emits clamp01(0.3 * sampleCoverage) for the low-information case. The plumbing to act on the number is what is missing.
acceptance_criteria: view.confidence reaches metric confidence (e.g. as a multiplier on view-fit) or gates the exclusion decision, so that a low-confidence view classification cannot simultaneously hard-exclude six metrics and grant ~1.0 confidence to two others. Demo 2's armSwingSymmetry/stepWidth stop reading High confidence off a 0.077 view call.
close_reason:
Verified live 2026-08-29, 3 trials x 3 clips, real GPU, branch worktree-agent-a22fa3ff4db5cd30e @ a2a0143. Bit-identical to baseline on every metric value, confidence, view, sampling, scale-pass field and evidence status — the change's own central falsifiable prediction, confirmed.

WHAT SHIPPED: a view PLAUSIBILITY distribution (src/heuristics/viewPlausibility.ts). Each signal ramps linearly across the band between the two views' own thresholds (BSR: side-support 1 at <=0.30 -> 0 at >=0.55; SER: front-support 1 at <=0.40 -> 0 at >=0.80); a view's plausibility is the PRODUCT of its two supports — the continuous form of the existing 'both signals must agree' rule — and 'ambiguous' takes the remainder. computeFormHeuristics resolves the viewFitTable against that distribution once, rather than passing a bare label to eleven metrics. ZERO new constants: only the four existing view thresholds in their existing roles.

STRUCTURAL HALF OF THE ACCEPTANCE: MET. Gating can no longer simultaneously hard-exclude six metrics and grant ~1.0 to two others from a number nothing reads, because both directions now flow from one distribution.

*** DEMO-2 HALF OF THE ACCEPTANCE: DELIBERATELY NOT MET, AND I AGREE WITH THE REASONING. ***
The ticket asked that demo2's armSwingSymmetry/stepWidth stop reading High confidence. They still read 0.977/1.000. The argument, which I accept: demo2's plausibility is exactly one-hot front (BSR 0.5507 >= 0.55 kills side support; SER 0.3389 <= 0.40 gives full front support), because side fails BOTH its conditions by more than 2x — needs BSR<=0.30, got 0.5507; needs SER>=0.8, got 0.3389. The marginality of the FRONT label is not evidence for SIDE, and only the latter could rightly degrade a front-primary metric. Degrading armSwingSymmetry there would have deleted a metric whose evidence images plainly show both arms, on a hypothesis the geometry excludes. Meeting the criterion would have required a coefficient justified only by producing the requested number on one clip.

NO OBSERVABLE IMPROVEMENT TODAY. This is a no-op on all three reference clips because all three commit to a label (one-hot plausibility -> the table returns by reference). It is observable only on a clip reading 'ambiguous', of which this repo has none. The mechanism's correctness therefore rests on its 27 new unit tests, not on live footage. Recorded plainly rather than presented as a win.

Why it still ships: gating from a distribution is strictly more correct than from a label; it is proven zero-risk; and it is INDEPENDENT of the strides-2iw defect, since plausibility ramps linearly and never calls the saturating marginAwayFromZero that 2iw is about. The two are complementary — 2iw fixes the reported confidence number, this fixes what gating reads.

RESIDUAL MOVED TO strides-2iw (raised to P1): the 0.077 is a broken measurement, not genuine doubt. Front-view confidence is structurally capped at ~0.51-0.609 by the BSR margin saturating at ~2x the signal's anatomical maximum, so no front clip can ever clear 0.7.

Also corrected by this work: stepWidthCm is front-PRIMARY, not sagittal — its demo2 exclusion is a null value (no MoveNet scale), not view fit. So demo2 has FIVE view-excluded metrics, not six as my 2026-08-19 review stated.

openspec change propagate-view-confidence-to-metric-gating validates --strict. 2 ADDED + 6 MODIFIED requirements; the 6 are one identical one-clause rewording each, listed in design.md D6 with a reconcile-before-archiving warning for strides-5x1. NOT archived. tsc/eslint clean, 1238 tests green.

title: Evidence centring makes an unannotated bystander the visual subject of multiperson kneeFlexion
description:
Found by UX review of strides-e9b (centre-evidence-crop-on-subject), by looking at rendered thumbnails at their real 130px inline size.

On e2e/fixtures/multiperson-track.mp4, kneeFlexion's 320px crop now trades roughly 90px of dead pavement for a man in a white t-shirt, walking, FULLY IN FRAME, DEAD CENTRE, carrying no annotation at all. At 130px he is the most legible human in the picture — on a card whose caption reads 'Two frames of the same runner blended into one image.'

The measured runner sits at the far left and is cut by the left edge, with a cyan joint dot and part of the amber knee arc literally on x=0. That clipping is PRE-EXISTING and unchanged; what strides-e9b changed is the vertical position, which promoted the bystander from a pair of legs at the top edge into the centre of the frame.

This is the same failure mode strides-e9b was written to fix (GitHub #71 item 2 — a bystander reading as a second body in a ghosted composite), recurring in a different image. Shipping it that way is defensible only because it lands on a test fixture rather than either demo clip, and because both user-facing demo clips improved or held.
design:
Related root cause to strides-830: both are the general framing-convergence behaviour the code review asked to be documented — when the floor binds and the runner fits inside it on both axes, the crop is fully determined by the subject and the metric's own crop-keypoint set stops affecting framing at all. Any clip where the runner is under 320px reproduces this for every floor-bound metric.

Candidate direction NOT chosen in e9b, recorded by the code reviewer: shift the crop by the MINIMUM distance that brings subjectBox inside, rather than fully centring. That preserves per-metric framing, but is weaker on e9b's actual defect (55px of leftover background beside the runner on Demo 2, versus full centring's 27.6px). A rule that varies by how much slack exists, or by metric scale, would need measurement across more than these three clips.
acceptance_criteria: At 130px inline, the annotated runner is the most visually prominent person in the multiperson kneeFlexion thumbnail. Verified by pulling the image from the DOM and looking at it downscaled, not by a numeric proxy. Demo 1 and Demo 2 framing must not regress.
notes: Do NOT fix by moving EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX (320) — frozen, sized for viewer-side display legibility. Sibling findings: strides-830 (footStrikePattern), strides-9wp (fresh-process determinism).
close_reason: Same as strides-830: filed from a UX review of strides-e9b's crop-centring implementation, which exists nowhere in git. Not current behaviour on main. Re-file if e9b is re-implemented.

title: Evidence crop for footStrikePattern reframes to whole-body on MoveNet, clipping the shoe
description: Discovered while implementing strides-e9b (centre-evidence-crop-on-subject). On e2e/fixtures/multiperson-track.mp4, footStrikePattern's 320px floor-bound crop now centres vertically on the subject's resolvable extent, which moves it up ~104px and reframes a foot close-up into a whole-body shot with the sole of the shoe clipped at the bottom edge. Every measured keypoint (left_ankle/left_knee) and every drawn annotation mark is still inside the crop, verified by magnifying the image, so this is not a regression by the stated bar - but the picture now shows the runner rather than the shoe it is about. Root cause is frameSubjectBox's documented backend dependence: COMMON_KEYPOINT_NAMES' four heel/foot-index names are MediaPipe-only and resolve unrecoverable on MoveNet, so the subject is understood as head-to-ankle and the crop bottom lands 16.7px below the ankle. Fixing it means either a metric-specific framing rule or a foot extent MoveNet does not produce; both are larger decisions than e9b. Demo 1's two footStrikePattern images are byte-identical before/after (their subject is wider than the crop on both axes), so this only shows up where the floor binds.
notes:
UX REVIEW 2026-08-19 strengthens this from 'character change' to a real communication regression, and answers the judgement call explicitly: it IS a worse explanation of the number on the card.

Not a correctness issue — every mark is confirmed inside the crop. The problem is where the eye goes at DISPLAY size. On main the frame was legs + planted shoe filling the upper half, and at 130px you could see a shoe with an amber line running to it: the image said 'foot'. After centring, at 130px it is a generic photo of a runner against a fence, the foot construction is an indistinct smudge in the bottom-left corner, and the toe is clipped.

SECOND COST, not previously recorded: the same metric now looks completely DIFFERENT across clips. Demo 1 keeps a tight shin-and-shoe close-up (those two images are byte-identical to main); multiperson gets a full figure. A user seeing both would not recognise them as the same kind of evidence.

Reviewer's framing, which is the useful one: footStrikePattern is the one metric whose subject is genuinely a BODY PART, so centring on the whole body is the wrong default for it specifically. The fix is a metric-scale framing rule, deliberately NOT attempted in strides-e9b because a per-metric carve-out chosen at review time without measurement is the same 'tuning against one clip' that ticket forbade.
close_reason: Describes a code state absent from the repo. Filed from a UX review of strides-e9b's crop-centring implementation; frameSubjectBox exists on no branch, no worktree, no stash, and computeEvidenceCropRect on main is unchanged. Re-file if e9b is re-implemented.

title: Evidence crop floor pulls a bystander into armSwingSymmetry's limb crop
description: GitHub #71 item 2. On Demo 2 (park-approach.mp4), reproduced on EVERY trial: armSwingSymmetry's left-side exemplar crop sits at the EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX=320 floor around shoulder/elbow/wrist and swallows a background bystander in a yellow shirt standing to the subject's right. He reads as a second body in a ghosted composite. Clip-specific in its particulars, systematic in its cause: the floor inflates a small limb box until it takes in whatever is beside the subject, and a ghost composite makes the extra person look like part of the blend.
design:
CORRECTED 2026-08-19 after a sizing pass — the original note here named the wrong data source. Do not plan against it.

WRONG (what this ticket first said): 'use the bounding boxes from src/results/retroactivePersonSelection.ts'. That data does NOT reach the planning layer. selectRetroactivePersonOfInterest computes per-frame boxes via deriveBoundingBox purely to score/segment/select one track, then DISCARDS them; the only thing it returns is PersonSelectionDiagnostics, an aggregated dev-console-only object with no per-frame box surviving. It does not import into evidenceFrames.ts in either direction. There is also NO per-frame 'other people' data anywhere — RobustPoseFrame and PoseSample carry no boundingBox field, and detection is single-person per frame at the detector level. There is structurally no bystander to look up.

RIGHT (the mechanism the available data actually supports): the SUBJECT'S OWN full-body extent IS derivable at every instant. Each RobustPoseFrame carries a dense keypoints array — one entry per COMMON_KEYPOINT_NAMES (all 15), always present, each tagged detected/interpolated/unrecoverable. computeEvidenceCropRect (evidenceFrames.ts:583-601) and frameCropBox (:376-384) only ever read the subset named in exemplar.cropKeypoints, which for a limb metric is 3 points. Nothing stops the crop math from ALSO consulting the frame's complete keypoint set to derive the subject's own extent and shape the floor-inflated crop against it. The frame object is already in hand — no new data path, no second detection pass.

HARD CONSTRAINT UNCHANGED: do NOT raise or lower EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX (320). It was sized against the VIEWER for display legibility, per its own doc comment — it is not a detector concern and moving it to dodge one bystander is tuning a constant against one clip.

SPEC NOTE: openspec/specs/results-view/spec.md:605 'Requirement: Evidence frames are planned purely, then extracted from a detached video element' is the only requirement describing crop derivation. It is ALREADY STALE independent of this ticket — its text describes padding+clamping only and never mentions EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH / isTooFarApartPair, which already shipped for #71 item 1. Decide whether to catch that up in the same delta or leave it; flag the call either way. Its scenario 'A subject near the frame edge yields a valid crop' constrains any change here.

PRECEDENT: EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH=2.5 / isTooFarApartPair (evidenceFrames.ts:134, :620-641, :657-664, wired in at :816-823) is the item-1 fix and is the model for how a guard of this kind is expressed here — a pure geometric ratio computed from data already in hand.
acceptance_criteria: The armSwingSymmetry left-side exemplar on Demo 2 no longer contains the bystander, verified by pulling the rendered image out of the DOM and LOOKING at it — not by a numeric proxy. Crop side and aspect-ratio invariants still hold (single shared aspect ratio across all metrics; a subject near a frame edge still yields a valid clamped rect). Demo 1 and multiperson coverage do not regress. EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX is unchanged.
notes:
STATUS RESET 2026-08-29: was marked in_progress, but the implementation is NOT in the repo. frameSubjectBox / crop centring exists on no branch, no worktree, no stash, no dangling ref; computeEvidenceCropRect (evidenceFrames.ts:626) is unchanged and 'centre' appears nowhere in the file. Three tickets filed from a UX review of that lost work (strides-830, strides-hle, strides-2jd) were closed as not-current-behaviour; re-file them if this is re-implemented. Start from scratch against the CORRECTED design note above (subject extent from the frame's full 15-keypoint set, NOT retroactivePersonSelection).
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-30 on worktree-agent-a59df29571a3c8276 (branch fast-forwarded to main c088f16 first
— the worktree was 22 commits behind, including 223 lines of evidenceFrames.ts). Openspec change:
place-floored-evidence-crop-on-subject (NOT archived).

MECHANISM (the corrected design note, followed): computeEvidenceCropRect now derives the subject's own
extent from the frame's complete keypoint set (frameSubjectExtentBox, every COMMON_KEYPOINT_NAMES entry
that resolves, unioned across the drawn frames) and, where the DISPLAY FLOOR made the crop wider than
the subject on an axis, centres the crop on the subject along that axis instead of on the limb
(subjectCentredCropRect). Only x/y move; side never does, so evidencePairCropGrowth, isTooFarApartPair
and cropSidePx cannot observe it. EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX unchanged at 320; no constant moved and no
new tunable constant introduced.

Two conditions per axis, both measured as load-bearing:
  (1) paddedSide <= subjectExtent[A] < side  — the floor, not the padding, is what made it wider.

title: Evidence photograph carries no base/ghost signal, so the annotated skeleton contradicts it
description:
RCA 2026-08-18. On the verticalOscillation evidence thumbnail (Demo 2), the solid cyan skeleton reads as sitting on the wrong body.

Not a data bug. Verified live (real GPU, ANGLE Metal Renderer): base=1.017683s (peak), ghost=0.850850s (valley), matching the label. Peak/valley ground-truthed from park-approach.mp4 keyframes with camera drift (dy=+10px, template-matched on a background patch) and approach scale (cap width ~90px in both) ruled out. Skeleton registration verified by drawing each skeleton's shoulder-line y onto the reconstructed single instants: the solid skeleton lands exactly on the peak instant's shoulders.

Root cause: the two layers use incompatible emphasis models.
- Photograph is SYMMETRIC. extractFrames.ts draws base at globalAlpha 1 onto a transparent canvas then ghost at 0.5 over it; source-over collapses to exactly 0.5*base + 0.5*ghost. Measured, not reasoned: a blend-weight sweep against the real canvas peaks at exactly 50/50 (17.74 dB, vs 16.14 base-only and 16.42 ghost-only). Intent is stated only in a code comment (evidenceFrames.ts:76-85) and the archived metric-frame-evidence design.md:826-831.

So the caption says 'ghosted against' and the skeleton picks a winner, but the picture picks none. The reader resolves it from whatever cue is strongest, and on this image that cue points at the ghost (see the head-clipping bead).

Remediation sketch (not implemented): split the shared EVIDENCE_GHOST_OPACITY into a photographic ghost weight and an annotation ghost weight, and drop the photographic one below 0.5 so the base body genuinely reads solid. title: Evidence seek lands one frame early on multiperson-track.mp4 (ac9.4 residual)
description:
Live verification for strides-ac9.5 measured residual annotation misregistration on all three clips by ffmpeg/PSNR argmax against the app's own un-annotated evidence canvas (temporary dev probe, added-measured-reverted).

RESULT
- Demo 1 (25 fps): delta 0. 40.80 dB at the correct frame vs 21.36/21.02 either side.
- Demo 2 (59.94 fps): delta 0. 25.08 dB vs 23.16/22.92.
- e2e/fixtures/multiperson-track.mp4 (60 fps): delta -1 frame (-16.7 ms), on BOTH single-instant exemplars.
  - footStrike t=2.416667 -> correct ffmpeg frame 143; argmax 142 (16.84 dB vs 15.33 / 13.95).
  - footStrike t=2.766667 -> correct frame 164; argmax 163 (15.46 dB vs 13.74 / 13.60).

NOT AN APP RACE. A pure Chromium seek to the identical target, no app involved, produces a
BYTE-IDENTICAL canvas: video.currentTime = 2.3833336666666667 renders the same pixels as
currentTime = 2.375 (interior of frame 142), while 2.3833343 renders the same pixels as
2.3916667 (interior of frame 143). The flip point sits in a ~0.6 microsecond window just above
frame 143's presentation timestamp.

MECHANISM. resolveEvidenceSeekOffsetSeconds is arithmetically correct — it lands the seek on the
target frame's exact presentation timestamp by construction. Chromium quantises media timestamps
to integer microseconds, and on this clip its stored timestamp for the target frame ends up 1 us
above the value the double-precision subtraction produces, so the seek resolves to the preceding
frame. On Demo 1 and Demo 2 the same arithmetic happens to land at or above the stored value, so
they are exact. Whether a clip is affected is a property of its timescale and the specific
sample, not of the code.

DO NOT FIX BY PICKING AN EPSILON. Nudging the seek target by a sub-frame constant is the same
'pick a number' trap CLAUDE.md documents for DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_SEEK_OFFSET_SECONDS: too small and
it does nothing, too large and it overshoots to the next frame on clips that are currently exact.
A defensible fix would derive the seek target in the same integer tick domain the container uses
(cts ticks minus elst media_time ticks, divided once), so no intermediate double subtraction
exists to round the wrong way.

COST. The pictured frame is one frame (16.7 ms) earlier than the frame the analysis measured, on
this clip only. Visually the joints still land on the limb; it is a measurable residual, not a
visible defect.

Repro: openspec harness in CLAUDE.md; probe recipe is the [evidence-seek] / raw-canvas pair
described in the metric-frame-evidence design doc, plus scripts in the session scratchpad.
close_reason: Won't fix by prior decision: the -1 frame is Chromium integer-microsecond quantisation, reproduces with a bare seek and no app involved, and CLAUDE.md records it as explicitly not to be fixed with an epsilon. The seek arithmetic is correct and lands on the frame boundary by construction.

title: Annotation makes GitHub #71's whole-frame crop defect unmistakable
description:

title: Grafted exemplars carry the scale pass's instants but not its frames
description:
The root cause behind strides-ac9.7's option-(a) workaround. Filed so the workaround is not mistaken for a fix.

scalePassGraft.ts:43-50 records the seam plainly: a grafted exemplar carries the SCALE PASS's instants, but 'the only frames any consumer holds are the primary pass's'. So stepWidthCm and verticalOscillationCm get their joint positions and hip polarity resolved off a MoveNet frame snapped within tolerance — never the MediaPipe frame that actually measured them.

At a near-frontal step-width strike the two hips sit a few pixels apart and the two detectors can order them oppositely, so the plan can carry the INVERSE polarity, labelling a crossover strike as landing on its own side — contradicting stepWidth.ts:273-277's own crossover caveat in the same viewport.

ac9.7 mitigated by suppressing POLARITY (not geometry) for GRAFTED_METRICS. That is correct and cheap, but it is a workaround at the consumer, not a fix at the seam.

The clean fixes, per ac9.7: either a grafted exemplar carries its own pass's frames, or the graft drops when no primary frame corroborates it. Both are scalePassGraft.ts's business, and both are larger than any ticket in epic strides-ac9.

Note this seam previously carried only a coarse crop box, where a few pixels are invisible. ac9.6 was the first change to push a polarity through it — so the seam got riskier without anyone widening it.

- [ ] A grafted metric's annotation geometry derives from the frames that measured it, or the graft is dropped when unsupported
- [ ] ac9.7's GRAFTED_METRICS polarity suppression can be removed, or is documented as permanently correct

description:

title: Footstrike timing carries a +0.11s systematic lag on Demo 1 — measure duty factor, do not fit a constant
description:
derive-footstrike-timing-from-bounce-phase puts touchdown a quarter fitted period before each hip-bounce low point. Against keyframe-confirmed onsets on Demo 1 the emitted instants land at +0.12/+0.10/+0.12/+0.10s -- a systematic +0.11s (2.75 frames at 25fps), with a within-clip spread of only 0.020s against the ankle detector's 0.340s.

The closed form predicts far less: lag = (stance - T/2)/2, which from Demo 1's stance durations is 0.4-1.4 frames. The gap is weakness W1 -- the hip's low point trails midstance by more than the model allows -- and it is confirmed to be a property of the signal rather than the estimator: the fitted low points (4.361/5.019/5.677s) land on real local maxima of that run's raw hip-y trace (4.36/5.00/5.64-5.72).

DO NOT fix this with a constant offset. That is the exact mistake strides-da8's proof was against: the right value is a function of the runner's own duty factor and of how far their hip low point trails their midstance, and neither is measured today. A next attempt should measure the duty factor -- stance is observable from the same ankle-x stationarity that corroborated the onset correction (325 px/s against the hip's 1617 px/s on Demo 1) -- and derive the correction from it, or show that it cannot be measured reliably enough to use.

Full numbers: openspec/changes/derive-footstrike-timing-from-bounce-phase/design.md D3, D6/W1, D11.2.
acceptance_criteria: Either a derived (not fitted) correction that reduces the systematic lag on all three clips without widening the within-clip spread, or a measurement showing the duty factor cannot be recovered reliably enough to derive one. No constant offset either way.

title: stepWidthCm's paired exemplar omits measuredSide, so its caliper is never drawn
description:

exemplar is affected -- and the paired branch is the common case.

Found while measuring strides-zp6 (which came back a clean null: the select-then-score shape
that ticket describes costs no clip an exemplar today). This is a DIFFERENT defect, and it is

title: armSwing frequency band floor excludes cadences below ~144 spm
description:
One arm swing spans one STRIDE, so its frequency is half the step rate, but armSwingSymmetry fits over the SHARED spectralFitMinFrequencyHz/Max band (1.2-4.0 Hz) which was sized for the per-step hip bounce. A runner below roughly 144 spm therefore has their true arm-swing frequency below the band floor entirely and cannot be fitted correctly.

Demo 1 is exactly that case: cadence 91.2 spm implies a 0.76 Hz arm swing; its fits land at 1.70 Hz (left) and 1.54 Hz (right) with R2 0.385/0.383. It is side-view/tier-3 excluded so nothing is shown, but a slow front-view clip would hit this in the UI.

Halving the band to 0.6-2.0 Hz was measured and REJECTED in fit-arm-swing-amplitude (design D3): on Demo 2 it is a wash (agrees within one grid step, 0.3% of amplitude) but its secondPeakRatio is strictly worse (0.13->0.25 left, 0.31->0.69 right), and on BOTH side-view clips it lands on its own grid FLOOR at 0.60 Hz with barely one observed cycle - a grid-edge artifact that looks like an answer. Do not re-litigate by just picking a wider band.

A next attempt needs either a per-metric band that is bounded BELOW by observed cycles rather than by a fixed floor, or a real slow-cadence front-view clip to calibrate against. Neither exists today.

title: Two async callers have no rejection handler, so a throw surfaces as an unhandled rejection
description:
Flagged by strides-k03's agent, deliberately not fixed there because it is a behaviour change in files that refactor otherwise did not touch.

useClipPoster.ts:41 and useSessionEvidence.ts:280 both call an async derivation with no rejection handler. Neither derivation is supposed to throw - every failure they know about resolves to null - so a throw is by definition a bug, and today it surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection rather than anywhere a developer will see it.

Note strides-k03 CORRECTED the related doc rather than adding a catch, and the reasoning transfers: an existing test deliberately pins deriveClipPoster REJECTING when URL.createObjectURL throws, and pins that the shared queue survives it. Swallowing the rejection at the call site would leave the poster null either way while erasing the only signal the bug exists.

So the question here is not 'add a catch' but 'where should an unexpected throw become visible' - a dev-only console line, an error boundary, or leaving it as an unhandled rejection on purpose and documenting that. It is a repo-wide pattern (two sites, and EvidenceGallery.tsx had a third before it was deleted), so decide once and apply to both.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on where an unexpected derivation throw becomes visible, applied consistently at both sites. The existing test pinning deriveClipPoster's rejection and queue survival still passes.
