title: demo1 trunkLean evidence appears in only 1 of 3 runs after the pair-fallback walk
description:
Follow-up from strides-2i1, measured 2026-08-29, 3 trials, real GPU, branch verify-all.

After the fallback walk landed:
  multiperson trunkLean: all-gated-out -> planned:1 on 3 of 3 trials (cropGrowth 2.448)
  demo1 trunkLean:       all-gated-out -> planned:1 on 1 of 3 trials (cropGrowth 1.866)
So demo1's trunkLean card gains and loses its image between otherwise-identical runs. The image it does produce is good (verified by eye: runner visible at both instants 5.56/5.08 s, correct joints, amber trunk segment and vertical reference).

Cause is presumably that run-to-run sampling variance changes the candidate set, and on 2 of 3 runs none of the <=36 pairs reachable within EXEMPLAR_PAIR_ENDS_PER_SIDE = 6 is admissible.

DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY RAISING THE BOUND UNTIL DEMO 1 PASSES. That is tuning to a result, which this repo has recorded and rejected twice. The bound must be justified by what fraction of admissible pairs it can REACH, not by whether one clip emits.

The measurement that would justify a change, and which nobody has taken: on a failing run, instrument the walk to report the growth of every one of the 36 evaluated pairs plus how many candidates were bounded out. If admissible pairs (growth < 2.5) exist just outside the 6-per-side cut, widening is warranted and the new bound follows from the observed rank at which admissible pairs start appearing. If every pair in the whole candidate set exceeds 2.5, the bound is irrelevant and demo1's trunkLean extremes genuinely cannot be co-cropped on those runs — which is an honest null, and the ticket should close as working-as-intended.

Note the walk is cheap (one sort per side plus a 36-element sort, constant in candidate count), so cost is not the constraint on widening — justification is.

EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH (2.5) must not move; it is bracketed by two measured images at 2.190 and 5.815.
acceptance_criteria: Either the per-side bound is changed with a measurement showing at which rank admissible pairs begin appearing on demo1's failing runs, or the ticket closes as working-as-intended with the measurement showing no admissible pair exists. EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH unchanged either way.
notes:
RE-MEASURED UNDER THE FRESH-PROCESS REGIME (2026-08-29, strides-b0y). Verdict: (a) with a caveat -- the symptom is a harness artifact, but it is NOT stochastic and the failing state still exists and is reproducible on demand.

SETUP. main @ 4173f1c, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro, asserted, never SwiftShader), scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs --arm base={} --evidence, dev server on the derived per-checkout port with the nonce identity check green. Nothing in src/ touched; EXEMPLAR_PAIR_ENDS_PER_SIDE and EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH unchanged.

FRESH PROCESS PER TRIAL -- demo1 trunkLean emits 16 of 16.
Two independent 8-trial invocations (--clips demo1,multiperson --trials 8 --evidence). Per-trial [evidence-coverage] for demo1 trunkLean, run 1 and run 2, all 8 trials each:
  status           planned x8 | planned x8
  reason           null x8    | null x8
  cropGrowth       1.8659748463472035  (identical, 16/16)
  quality          0.5670389655365092  (identical, 16/16)
  timestamp        5.56                (identical, 16/16)
  pairedTimestamp  5.08                (identical, 16/16)
  demotedFromPair  false               (identical, 16/16)
The two runs whole reports diff on exactly one line per clip: elapsedMs. So the exemplar this ticket calls "the good image" (runner visible at 5.56/5.08, cropGrowth 1.866) is the ONLY thing demo1 produces in the fresh regime. Control: multiperson trunkLean is likewise planned 16/16 at cropGrowth 2.28947904030852, quality 0.6916884703221782.

THE 1-IN-3 SYMPTOM REPRODUCES EXACTLY UNDER --reuse-browser, AND IT IS BIMODAL, NOT RANDOM.
One invocation, --clips demo1 --trials 6 --reuse-browser --evidence:
  trial                              1        2        3        4        5        6
  personSelection.detectedSamplesIn  66       65       65       65       65       65
  personSelection.segmentCount       4        3        3        3        3        3
  metrics.kneeFlexion.value          120.690  116.924  116.924  116.924  116.924  116.924
  evidence trunkLean.status          planned  gated    gated    gated    gated    gated
  evidence trunkLean.cropGrowth      1.86597  -        -        -        -        -
("gated" = status no-evidence, reason all-gated-out.) Trial 1 is bit-identical to the fresh regime. Trials 2-6 are bit-identical to EACH OTHER at a different state. So "1 of 3 runs" was "the 1 cold-process trial of 3" -- this ticket premise that run-to-run sampling variance changes the candidate set is right about the mechanism and wrong about the source: the variance is browser-process warmth, not GPU non-determinism, and it is a two-state switch.

WHAT ACTUALLY DIFFERS BETWEEN THE TWO STATES. detectedFrames is 53 in both, so this is not a throughput loss. detectedSamplesIn is 66 (cold) vs 65 (warm) -- ONE detection -- and that one frame re-partitions the track (segmentCount 4 -> 3), which changes the surviving frame set that trunkLean candidate instants are drawn from. In the warm set, no pair reachable within EXEMPLAR_PAIR_ENDS_PER_SIDE = 6 is admissible; in the cold set the rank-1 pair is (5.56, 5.08) at cropGrowth 1.866, comfortably inside EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH = 2.5.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE.
- It settles the framing: there is no flakiness to chase. Under the regime this repo now measures in (fresh process per trial, the default since strides-9wp), demo1 trunkLean emits deterministically, 16/16, with a good image. Nobody needs to widen a bound to make demo1 pass, and the "1 of 3" observation should not be cited again as evidence that the bound is too tight.
- It does NOT prove the bound is right. A reproducible failing state still exists: the warm process. If anyone wants the measurement this ticket acceptance criteria ask for -- the growth of all <=36 evaluated pairs on a failing run, and how many candidates were bounded out -- it is now cheap and deterministic to obtain, because the failing run no longer has to be waited for: instrument the walk and drive `node scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs --arm base={} --clips demo1 --trials 2 --reuse-browser --evidence` and read trial 2. That is a stable, repeatable failing candidate set.
- Honest caveat on which state is real: fresh-process pins every trial to the COLD operating point. A real user browser is warm. So the warm state is arguably the more representative one, and it is the one that gates out. That is an argument for taking the instrumented measurement above seriously, not for treating this ticket as closed by the fresh reading alone.

RECOMMENDATION. Do not close as working-as-intended on the strength of the fresh 16/16 alone, and do not touch EXEMPLAR_PAIR_ENDS_PER_SIDE. Either (i) take the per-pair growth measurement against the reused-regime warm state described above and let the bound follow from the observed rank at which admissible pairs appear, or (ii) close with the explicit reasoning that this repo measures in the fresh regime, demo1 emits there deterministically, and the warm-state failure is out of scope. Whichever, this ticket is no longer blocked on strides-b0y.
MEASURED AND CLOSED AS WORKING-AS-INTENDED (2026-08-29). The per-side bound is NOT the
constraint that binds, and no value of it -- including unbounded -- changes the warm-state
outcome. EXEMPLAR_PAIR_ENDS_PER_SIDE and EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH both unchanged.

SETUP. main @ 0b1b197, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro, asserted), dev server on
the derived port 5297 with the nonce identity check green. Temporary probe
(exemplarSelectionProbe.experimental.ts + one dev-only log in trunkLean.ts + one in

shipped bound never reaches could still be scored. Validated against the shipped path: on the

cropGrowth 1.8659748463472035, 5.56/5.08 -- the exact figures in this ticket's own notes.

REPRODUCED THE FAILING STATE. --clips demo1 --trials 2 --reuse-browser --evidence:
trial 1 (cold) trunkLean planned, cropGrowth 1.86597; trial 2 (warm) all-gated-out. Warm
primary pass: 59 candidates, 29 eligible high ends, 30 eligible low ends, median 13.8206 deg,
MAD 3.3507 -- against cold's 29/29, median 13.2968, MAD 3.0158.

THE <=36 EVALUATED PAIRS ON THE WARM RUN. 36 of 869 unbounded pairs are in bound; 23 high ends
and 24 low ends are bounded out. Growth by (highRank, lowRank):

  hR\lR      0        1        2        3        4        5     quality
    0    6.7448   6.6264   6.6932   6.2138   5.5261   6.1094   0.55534  <- only rank clearing 0.5
    1    6.7601   6.6416   6.7087   6.2294   5.5407   6.1250   0.46203
    2    3.6222   3.5369   3.5462   3.0348   2.5421   2.9274   0.45866
    3    6.6265   6.5094   6.5473   6.0076   5.4131   5.8989   0.44535
    4    2.9637   2.8854   2.8825   2.3644*  1.9128*  2.2563*  0.40969
    5    3.2281   3.1470   3.1490   2.6336   2.1655*  2.5258   0.39506
  (* growth < EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH = 2.5)

Four in-bound pairs are admissible by growth. Every one of them scores 0.40969 or 0.39506 --
BELOW MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY = 0.5 -- so attachPairAlternates drops them before the walk exists,
and planExemplarWithFallback re-drops them. The six pairs that DO clear the quality gate all sit
at highRank 0 and run 5.53-6.74 growth.

WHY WIDENING CANNOT HELP, ON THE WHOLE CANDIDATE SET. Over all 869 unbounded pairs on the warm
run, exactly 11 clear quality 0.5 and ZERO of those 11 have growth < 2.5. All 11 share highRank
0; their partners span lowRank 0..10, so raising the bound from 6 to 11 adds exactly six more
pairs and every one still fails growth. The best quality found among ALL growth<2.5 pairs is
0.45866, and max quality among every out-of-bound pair is 0.55534 (a highRank-0 pair at growth
> 5). Quality is monotone non-increasing in per-side rank, so a wider bound can only ever add
LOWER-scoring pairs -- the two conditions are anti-correlated on this clip in this state.

So the ticket's second branch is reached, by a stronger route than it framed: it is not that
every pair exceeds 2.5 (367 of 869 do not), it is that every pair CLEARING THE QUALITY GATE
exceeds 2.5. demo1's trunkLean extremes genuinely cannot be co-cropped in the warm state, and
the per-side bound is irrelevant to that. Do not cite "1 of 3 runs" and do not widen the bound.

CONTRAST WITH COLD, which shows the bound is not marginal there either: 48 of 840 pairs clear
quality, 10 of those are admissible, and the winner is highRank 2 / lowRank 4 -- comfortably
inside 6.

ON WARM-VS-FRESH. The warm-state failure is ACCEPTABLE. It is one metric's evidence image on one
clip, degrading to no image rather than to a wrong one; the number, the caveat and the other six
planned images on that clip are unaffected. And it is honest: the frames that could share a crop
in that state are poorly detected (quality 0.39-0.46 is mostly detectionFactor), so emitting one
would be putting a picture under a measurement the tracking does not support. The fix that would
change it is moving MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY, which is out of bounds and would be tuning to a result.

FOLLOW-UP, if anyone wants demo1's warm trunkLean image back: the lever is the anti-correlation
itself -- the quality-clearing high end is at one screen position and the co-croppable ones at
another -- not any bound. That is a candidate-set question (which frames survive person
selection; one detection moves detectedSamplesIn 66->65 and re-partitions the track), not an
exemplar-ranking one.

landed (worktree-agent-a59df29571a3c8276, openspec place-floored-evidence-crop-on-subject), same
harness, headless Chromium on real GPU, fresh process, Demo 2.

The three crops, re-measured, and all three are BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after e9b:
  verticalOscillation    crop 719.9 px @ x 499  (ROI = 180x450 hip box, padded 720)
  verticalOscillationCm  crop 719.9 px @ x 499  (same image)
  stepWidth              crop 520.6 px @ x 576  (ROI = 85x325, padded 521)
The bead's numbers were 640/640/562; today's are 719.9/719.9/520.6 — the same crops, moved by
intervening exemplar-selection work, not by e9b.

WHY e9b's MECHANISM CANNOT HELP, and this is now arithmetic rather than a guess. e9b re-places a crop
only where the DISPLAY FLOOR is what made it wider than the subject: paddedSide <= subjectExtent < side.
All three of these have paddedSide == side (720, 720, 521) with the subject 283 px / 222 px wide, so
paddedSide <= subjectExtent is false on both axes and the rule declines. The bead called this exactly
right: these crops are not floor-bound, and the 320 px minimum never inflated them.

AND CENTRING WOULD MAKE ONE OF THEM WORSE, measured: had the floor-bound condition been dropped,
verticalOscillation on this clip WOULD qualify (subject 283 wide < 719.9; 768 tall >= 719.9) and
centring moves it +20 px TOWARD the yellow shirt — the crop currently sits slightly left of the
runner's centre and the runner's centre is on the bystander's side. A rule that helped the small crop
would have made the large one marginally worse.

Confirmed by looking, full resolution and at the real 144 CSS px inline size: the bystander is at the
right edge of the 719.9 px image (torso top-right, legs and white shoes below) and in the top-right
corner of the stepWidth image. At 144 px he is a yellow smudge; the runner fills the frame and
dominates completely. Materially less severe than the armSwingSymmetry case, exactly as filed.

These crops are large because their keypoint sets legitimately span the body, and the bystander stands
inside a correctly-sized crop of a real scene. No crop rule that keeps the measured region in frame can
exclude him — the only levers would be shrinking the crop below what the metric's own keypoints span,
or synthesising a bystander mask the pipeline has no data for (detection is single-person; no
RobustPoseFrame carries a bounding box). Closing.
close_reason: Working as intended: not floor-bound, so e9b's mechanism correctly declines; re-measured and confirmed by looking. Not fixable by cropping.

title: Demo 2 evidence is only deterministic with a fresh Chromium process per trial
description:
Discovered while verifying strides-e9b. Reusing ONE Chromium process across trials shifts Demo 2's sampling from trial 2 onward, producing a different armSwingSymmetry exemplar (t=1.468133, 398.7px crop, 449.4px subject) than a fresh process does (t=0.984317, 320px floor-bound crop, 264.7px subject). Only the fresh-process regime reproduces the coverage CLAUDE.md records for that clip.

This matters because it silently changes which code path a measurement exercises: in the reused-process regime the subject is WIDER than the crop, so the subject-centring rule correctly declines to fire — a driver reusing a browser would have measured 'no effect' for a fix that demonstrably works. Both regimes show the bystander, so the defect itself reproduces either way; it is the FIX that becomes invisible.

Same class of manufactured-false-negative as strides-zpb (foreign dev server on a shared port), which also fired for real this session.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md's 'Live-browser verification harness' section states that Demo 2 evidence trials need a fresh browser process per trial and why. Ideally scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs and any evidence driver launch per-trial rather than reusing a context.
notes: Correction: the determinism finding referenced in the close reason was filed as strides-b0y, not strides-nkv (the ID was written before the bead existed). See strides-b0y.
close_reason: Fixed on worktree-agent-a4af0b1f6ef5bc08b (3c0406b). scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs launches a fresh Chromium per trial by default; --reuse-browser opts back in. New --evidence flag captures [evidence-coverage] (waits for quiescence, not the first line). Reproduced both regimes: fresh = t=0.984317 / cropSidePx 320, no spread across 3 trials; --reuse-browser = 1.46813 [0.984317..1.46813] / 398.733 [320..398.733]. Confirmed a fresh browser.newContext() is NOT sufficient. Bonus finding: browser reuse is a large part of what CLAUDE.md calls GPU non-determinism — two independent 3-trial fresh runs on Demo 1 agreed on every field but elapsedMs, vs ~20 spread fields under reuse. Cost: 63-77ms/trial. CLAUDE.md updated per acceptance criteria. NOT pushed or merged.

title: Three more buildExemplars duplicates share a select-then-score shape
description:
Found while fixing strides-9mb (GitHub #70 finding 2). That ticket fixed the argmax-then-score shape in trunkLean.ts and overstriding.ts by extracting the shared selectRangePair primitive into exemplars.ts. A SECOND, structurally similar problem remains in three other metrics, in the representative role rather than the extreme role.

stepWidth.ts:62 and stepWidthCm.ts:61 are near-identical duplicates of each other. armSwingSymmetry.ts:160 (buildSideExemplar) has the same shape. All three SELECT first and SCORE second: selectOppositeSidePair picks the pair by closeness-to-median and only then scores it, with a fallback only when scoring returns null — not when it merely scores LOW. That is the same class of fragility strides-9mb fixed for the extreme role: coverage can hinge on one frame's detection status even though better-scoring candidates exist.

NOT known to be causing a live coverage loss today — unlike #70 finding 2, which was measured failing on Demo 1. This is a structural observation, so it needs measurement before it needs a fix.
design:
selectRangePair (exemplars.ts, added by strides-9mb) is the precedent for the extreme role: rank per end by quality, tie-break on extremeness. The representative role needs its own equivalent — rank candidates by quality among those acceptably close to the median, rather than picking the closest and then scoring it. Do not simply reuse selectRangePair; the roles invert the distance-from-median term and a representative pair has different pairing constraints (stepWidth needs OPPOSITE sides, which is why selectOppositeSidePair exists at all).

Also note bounceInstants.ts:208 buildBounceCycleExemplar is the in-repo precedent for extracting a shared helper across 3+ callers.
acceptance_criteria: First MEASURE: instrument the three metrics per the add-measure-revert cycle in CLAUDE.md and establish whether any of them is losing evidence on Demo 1, Demo 2 or multiperson-track.mp4 that a quality-ranked selection would recover. If none is, close with that finding recorded rather than refactoring for symmetry. If one is, fix it the way strides-9mb fixed the extreme role and verify live on real GPU via the LAST [evidence-coverage] console line.
notes:
Do not change MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY, EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX or the 3-MAD outlier bound. Related: GitHub #70 finding 1 (the 1.5-MAD gate being structurally unreachable for overstriding) is a separate, still-open design question.
MEASURED. The select-then-score shape costs NOTHING on any of the three clips today. Closing
with the finding rather than refactoring for symmetry, per this ticket's own acceptance
criteria. No code changed; MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY, EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX,
EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH and the 3-MAD bound all untouched.

SCOPE CORRECTION FIRST: armSwingSymmetry is NO LONGER one of the three. strides-gzl rewrote that
module the same day this was filed. buildSideExemplar no longer selects from a candidate set at
all -- the two instants come from selectBounceInstants on the FITTED phase (half a fitted period
apart, centred on the resolved span), scored on detection alone via describeDistribution([]).
There is nothing to rank, so there is no select-then-score. Only stepWidth.ts and stepWidthCm.ts
still carry the shape.

SETUP. main @ 0b1b197, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro, asserted), derived port
5297, nonce identity check green, fresh Chromium per trial (the default regime), 2 trials x
demo1/demo2/multiperson with --evidence. Temporary probe in
exemplarSelectionProbe.experimental.ts plus one dev-only call in each of the two metrics and one
log line in useSessionEvidence.ts -- added, measured and REVERTED; tree is byte-identical to
main. Per (clip, metric, pass) the probe recorded what the shipped rule selected and scored,
against the best quality reachable by ranking (a) the same adjacent opposite-side pairs, (b) ALL
opposite-side pairs, and (c) the single-strike fallback.

  clip         metric       elig  adj  usable  selected  bestAdj  bestAny  bestSingle  emits
  demo1        stepWidth       4    3   false    1.0000   1.0000   1.0000      1.0000   yes
  demo1        stepWidthCm     4    3   false    1.0000   1.0000   1.0000      1.0000   yes
  demo2        stepWidth       5    3    true    0.6667   0.6667   0.6667      1.0000   yes
  demo2        stepWidth       5    4    true    0.8049   0.8049   0.8049      1.0000   yes
  demo2        stepWidthCm     5    4    true    0.8504   0.8504   0.8504      1.0000   yes
  multiperson  stepWidth       5    4    true    0.9635   0.9635   0.9635      1.0000   yes
  multiperson  stepWidth       9    6    true    0.6667   0.6667   0.6667      1.0000   yes
  multiperson  stepWidthCm     9    6    true    0.6667   0.6667   0.6667      1.0000   yes
  (two rows per clip where the MoveNet primary and the MediaPipe scale pass saw different
  strike sets; both passes are shown. No trial-to-trial spread in the fresh regime.)

selected == bestAdjacent == bestAny in EVERY row: on these clips the closest-to-median opposite
pair IS the highest-quality one, so a quality-ranked selection would recover nothing. Worst
selected quality anywhere is 0.6667, which is 0.167 of headroom above MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY = 0.5
-- the shape has never come close to biting. Coverage confirms it: stepWidth is `planned` on
demo2 and `metric-excluded` (tier 3, no card) on demo1/multiperson; stepWidthCm is
`metric-excluded` on all three. Not one `all-gated-out` on either metric on any clip.

WHY IT DOESN'T BITE HERE, so nobody re-measures on the same footage: these are event-sampled
metrics with tiny candidate sets. demo1 has 4 eligible strikes -- below
MIN_INSTANCES_FOR_TYPICALITY = 5, so describeDistribution().usable is false, typicality is the
flat representative-role 1, and every quality collapses to detectionFactor = 1. demo2 and
multiperson have 5-9 strikes and 3-6 opposite adjacencies. With a candidate set that small,
"closest to median" and "highest quality" coincide by luck of numbers, not by design. The
structural risk is REAL and UNREALISED; a longer clip with more strikes and one badly-tracked
plant near the median is where it would show up, and no such clip is in this repo.

DEDUP VERDICT: WORTH DOING, but as its own ticket, not as a symmetry refactor bolted onto a null
measurement. The reason is measured, not aesthetic -- the two duplicates have ALREADY silently
diverged, and the divergence costs a drawn mark. See the follow-up bead filed alongside this
note: stepWidthCm's paired exemplar omits the measuredSide/pairedMeasuredSide that stepWidth's
otherwise-identical block supplies, so resolveInstantSide returns null and
buildStepWidthMarks bails at `if (side === null) return` before drawing the ankle-offset caliper
-- the mark that IS the measurement. Invisible today only because stepWidthCm is tier-3 on all
three clips. That is a behaviour change needing its own openspec change and its own live
verification, which is exactly why it is not being smuggled in here.
close_reason: Measured: the select-then-score shape costs no clip an exemplar today (selected == best-reachable quality on every clip and both passes; worst selected 0.6667 vs a 0.5 gate). armSwingSymmetry no longer has the shape at all after strides-gzl. Structural risk real but unrealised; closed with the finding rather than refactoring for symmetry, per the acceptance criteria. Dedup judged worth doing on its own merits and filed as strides-b5o with measured evidence.

title: Near-identical pair guard lets a 30ms pair through, so a ghosted image shows one pose
description:
Observed during the UX review of strides-c37; pre-existing pair selection, unrelated to the ghost weighting.

On e2e/fixtures/multiperson-track.mp4, kneeFlexion's exemplar pair is 3.52 s and 3.55 s — 30 ms, about two frames apart. The caption promises 'peak knee flexion, ghosted against the same leg near full extension' and the image shows a single pose.

EVIDENCE_NEAR_IDENTICAL_IOU = 0.98 (src/results/evidenceFrames.ts) is strict enough that a two-frame-apart pair survives instead of being demoted to a single frame. Demotion would caption honestly ('Shown as one frame: the paired instant was too similar to tell apart'), which is the behaviour that already exists for this case and simply is not being reached.

The 65/35 weighting makes it read even more like a single frame, but did not cause it — the alpha=0.50 control has the same pair.

Worth checking whether an elapsed-time floor is the right guard here rather than moving the IoU threshold: CLAUDE.md records that absolute separation and elapsed time both order the far-apart cases backwards, but this is the near-identical end, where a minimum instant separation may behave better than IoU on a subject that barely moves between adjacent frames.
acceptance_criteria: A pair whose two instants are too close in time to depict a difference is demoted to a single frame with the honest caption, rather than ghosted into an image that shows one pose. Verified on multiperson kneeFlexion without demoting pairs that currently ghost legibly.
notes: Confirmed still present after strides-c37's ghost-weight split (2026-08-29). multiperson kneeFlexion pairs base 3.516667 with ghost 3.55 — a 33 ms gap, cropGrowth 1.0 — and demo1 verticalOscillationCm pairs 5.36 with 5.04. The near-identical guard let the 33 ms pair through. Pre-existing at alpha=0.50; the 65/35 split neither causes nor masks it, though a near-identical pair is now slightly LESS visible as a double exposure since the ghost carries less weight.

title: Amber measurement marks run low-contrast over bright backgrounds at inline size
description:
Measured during the UX review of strides-c37 and confirmed PRE-EXISTING — within 0.1 of the alpha=0.50 control everywhere, so the ghost reweighting did not cause or worsen it.

Amber mark vs photograph contrast on the shipped composites: Demo 1 kneeFlexion 7.9:1, Demo 2 stepWidth 2.9:1, multiperson stride 1.7:1 (amber over the sunlit fence/path). WCAG wants 3:1 for UI components, so the multiperson case and Demo 2 stepWidth are below it.

Partly mitigated by the dark halo under every stroke — but at HALO_WIDTH_FRACTION = 0.005 the halo is sub-pixel once a 509 px canvas is drawn into a 144 px box, so the mitigation is materially weaker inline than at full resolution. That ratio is the thing to look at first.

Related but distinct from strides-c37's ghost-floor follow-up: this is about the MARK layer's contrast against the photograph, not about the ghost photograph's own visibility.
acceptance_criteria: Amber measurement marks reach at least 3:1 against the photograph beneath them at the real 144 CSS px inline size on all three test clips, including amber over the multiperson clip's sunlit fence.
notes: Baseline from strides-c37's post-merge verification (2026-08-29, 142 CSS px). Amber marks at 142 px: demo1 overstriding's two vertical hip guides and the foot arrow read; the trunkLean arc end-ticks and the VO bounce guides (~3 px apart displayed) do not resolve — matching CLAUDE.md's existing note. Dropping the photographic ghost to 0.35 did not change amber legibility either way; the amber sits over the base body, whose contrast went UP.

title: Evidence alt text does not convey the base/ghost emphasis the image now has
description:
Found by the UX review of strides-c37, out of scope there (captions and alt text were excluded).

Since strides-c37 the ghosted photograph is weighted 65/35 toward its base instant, so the image now carries a visual hierarchy: one instant is shown more strongly than the other. altFor (src/results/evidenceCaptions.ts) still says only '<Metric>: <label>. Two frames of the same runner blended into one image.' — the shape is stated, the emphasis is not.

A sighted reader gets 'this one is the subject' from the weighting and from the solid vs faded skeleton. A screen-reader user gets neither. The caption's 'X, ghosted against Y' already implies which instant is the subject, so this is a gap rather than a contradiction, but one clause in altFor would close it.

Note the linear read is otherwise fine and was checked: figure -> div[role=img][aria-label] -> figcaption carrying both timestamps. The label duplication between alt text and caption is pre-existing and unrelated.
acceptance_criteria: A non-visual reader can tell from the text alternative alone which of the two blended instants is the one the card's measurement is about.
notes:
CODE LANDED 2026-08-29, bead deliberately still OPEN pending its spec delta. altFor now appends 'the first instant named above is shown solid, the second faded behind it' to the blended shape sentence; src/results/evidenceCaptions.test.ts created (it did not exist - altFor/captionFor were covered only transitively by one MetricsPanel getByRole('img') name assertion, leaving the single-frame, demoted-pair and per-side branches unasserted). New assertion mutation-checked: reverting the sentence fails it. Full suite 86 files / 1308 tests green.

WHY THE SPEC DELTA IS DEFERRED: the governing requirement is results-view 'Evidence renders as annotated thumbnails inside the metric card', whose prose at ~line 989 says 'The text alternative MAY state the one-runner framing the caption omits' and whose scenario 'A ghosted thumbnail says it is one runner, not two people' ends '...its text alternative names the metric and, where the metric is per-side, the side'. That SAME requirement carries the 'at most one detached decoder open at a time' clause that strides-3uy modifies. Authoring a second MODIFIED block against it now would set up the exact silent clobber CLAUDE.md documents. Author the delta after strides-k03/3uy archives, extending both the prose and that scenario to cover the emphasis clause, then close.
close_reason: Fixed and merged 2026-08-29 (code 68b41d0; openspec change name-the-emphasised-instant-in-alt-text archived). altFor's blended shape sentence now reads 'Two frames of the same runner blended into one image: the first instant named above is shown solid, the second faded behind it.' Naming the FIRST instant is general rather than per-metric: every paired label this repo emits is 'X, ghosted against Y' with the base first (bounceInstants:236, kneeFlexion:117, overstriding:96, trunkLean:83), and that invariant is now stated in altFor's doc where a future author of a paired label will see it. Single-frame and demoted-pair images deliberately excluded - they carry ghost:null, nothing is blended, and claiming an emphasis would describe a second position not in the image (the same class of error as the reference-posture overlay the spec forbids); both exclusions asserted directly. Spec: MODIFIED 'Evidence renders as annotated thumbnails inside the metric card', extending both the text-alternative prose and the scenario 'A ghosted thumbnail says it is one runner, not two people'; the archived diff was verified to contain ONLY those two edits across an 88-line requirement body. Also created src/results/evidenceCaptions.test.ts, which did not exist - altFor/captionFor were covered only transitively by one MetricsPanel getByRole('img') assertion, leaving the single-frame, demoted-pair and per-side branches unasserted everywhere. Emphasis assertion mutation-checked.

title: Evidence ghost can vanish against a bright background at the 144px inline size
description:
Found by the UX review of strides-c37 (the 65/35 ghost weighting), and deliberately NOT fixed there.

On Demo 1 'kneeFlexion' the ghost instant sits at the right edge of the crop over bright grass and red track. At the real 144 CSS px card size it reads as a faint torso smear plus a three-dot amber stick with no leg under it — the results-view scenario 'The ghost stays visible as a body' failing on a single exemplar. Measured on the ghost's own pixels at the shipped alpha: its shin darkens the track by 24.5 levels (35 at the old alpha=0.50), its shorts tint the grass by +10 (+15 at 0.50).

The content and the annotation placement are both correct — recovering the ghost photograph per-pixel (by solving two composites at different alpha as two equations) shows a perfectly legible leg with the amber line right on it. What erases it is the weighting against a high-luminance background.

Milder second instance: Demo 2 'stepWidth', where the two instants overlap. At 144 px the ghost reads as whitish patches on the base's own thighs rather than a second position, so the second instant the caption promises is carried entirely by the marks. The alpha=0.50 control was only marginally better, so most of that one is the approach clip's overlap geometry.

Both exist ONLY at 144 px. At 320-640 px every exemplar passes comfortably, kneeFlexion included.

DO NOT fix by raising EVIDENCE_GHOST_BLEND_ALPHA. The discriminator is the background luminance the ghost happens to lie on, which alpha cannot see (design D2), and raising it would give back the emphasis on the other eleven exemplars. If this is worth closing it is a per-exemplar decision — e.g. a per-exemplar floor check on measured ghost contrast, or a crop that avoids placing the ghost over the brightest region.

Ghost-survival baseline for comparison (median per-pixel ghost contribution / share of ghost pixels above a 12-level visibility floor): demo1 16.3-19.4 / 84-89%, demo2 18.7-23.3 / 85-92%, multiperson 20.2-29.6 / 86-94%. Demo 1 is the weakest column.

Full record: openspec/changes/weight-evidence-ghost-below-base/design.md D10.
acceptance_criteria: Every ghosted exemplar on all three test clips keeps a ghost identifiable as a body at 144 CSS px, including Demo 1 kneeFlexion, without reducing the base's foreground emphasis on the exemplars that already read correctly.
notes: Fresh baseline from strides-c37's post-merge verification (2026-08-29, real GPU, 142 CSS px measured — not 144). At alpha=0.35 the ghost is at its weakest on light backgrounds: multiperson trunkLean (base 2.183333 right / ghost 2.65 left, over pale concrete) has the ghost nearly gone at 142 px — still a discernible body outline, but marginal. demo1 trunkLean and demo1/demo2 verticalOscillation all hold the ghost comfortably. The mechanism is in EVIDENCE_GHOST_BLEND_ALPHA's own doc: the shared background reproduces at alpha + (1-alpha) = 1 whatever the blend, so fading the ghost fades it against a background that never fades, and the floor is per-clip subject-against-background contrast.

title: Bounce-cycle evidence crop clips the base instant's head, handing the ghost the only legible face
description:
RCA 2026-08-18, contributing factor to the 'wrong body is ghosted' report.

BOUNCE_CONTEXT_KEYPOINTS (src/heuristics/bounceInstants.ts:56-61) is shoulders + knees, with the hip seed — no head keypoints. computeEvidenceCropRect unions both instants' boxes over those points and pads by EVIDENCE_CROP_PADDING_MULTIPLIER, so on a front-view clip the head sits above the padded top edge.

Because the base instant is the HIGHEST point of the bounce, it is exactly the instant whose head gets clipped. Verified on Demo 2: applying the app's own crop rect to both source frames, the peak instant (1.017683s) starts mid-face while the valley instant (0.850850s) keeps its whole head. The composite therefore contains one complete, legible face and it belongs to the GHOST. A reader anchors on that face as 'the runner', and the solid skeleton — correctly drawn ~31 output px above it, on the peak body — reads as mis-registered.

nose/left_ear/right_ear have been in COMMON_KEYPOINT_NAMES since the 2026-08-12 keypoint widening, so they are available to add to the context set.

Remediation sketch (not implemented): add the head keypoints to BOUNCE_CONTEXT_KEYPOINTS so both instants' heads survive the crop. Cheap and narrow, but it enlarges both boxes, so A/B it across Demo 1, Demo 2 and multiperson-track.mp4 for EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH (2.5) regressions before shipping — that threshold is pinned by measured images and must not be moved to accommodate this.
acceptance_criteria: Both instants of a bounce-cycle exemplar keep their heads inside the crop on all three test clips, and no pair that previously passed EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH starts failing it.
notes: Separate from the emphasis-model bead: fixing this removes the specific misleading cue on this image, but does not make 'which instant is ghosted' answerable from the photograph in general. Second contributing factor, unaddressed by either bead: separation is ~16 output px at the hip and ~31 at the shoulders on a 640px canvas, shown at 144 CSS px (commit 0325943 enlarged thumbnails from 112), so both skeletons and both amber guides merge into one blob inline.

title: Stale 'gallery' wording in src/ doc comments after EvidenceGallery was retired
description:
CLAUDE.md and openspec/specs are now correct (strides-91r), but 13 src/ files still describe the retired standalone gallery in doc comments. Docs-only cleanup; no behaviour change.

Confirmed occurrences include:
- src/video/extractFrames.ts:73 — 'a gallery image is on the ...' justifying EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX = 320
- src/video/evidenceSeekOffset.ts — module doc refers to threading a prop through MultiClipVideoSession/EvidenceGallery; EvidenceGallery.tsx no longer exists

Full list (grep -rli gallery src/): heuristics/exemplars.ts, video/extractFrames.ts, video/extractFrames.test.ts, video/evidenceSeekOffset.ts, video/evidenceSeekOffset.test.ts, results/evidenceFrames.ts, results/EvidenceCanvas.tsx, results/useSessionEvidence.ts, results/evidenceAnnotations.ts, results/evidenceCaptions.ts, results/multiClipAnalysis.ts, results/MetricsPanel.tsx, results/MultiClipVideoSession.tsx

Care needed on two: extractFrames.ts:73's 320 rationale is load-bearing reasoning that should be RESTATED for the inline thumbnail, not deleted — and the 320 floor is still an open image-quality defect (armSwingSymmetry swallows a bystander on Demo 2, gh #71). Do not change the constant here.

title: Poster and evidence keep separate decoder queues, so a global peak of 2 is possible
description:
Flagged by strides-0ok, deliberately not fixed there rather than widen scope.

posterFrame.ts and extractFrames.ts each own a module-level promise queue, so each guarantees at most one detached decoder OF ITS OWN KIND. Nothing coordinates the two, and a global peak of 2 concurrent 4K decoders is therefore structurally possible.

It never occurred in any measured run, and the reason is timing rather than design: posters are derived at clip-add time (all closed by ~950ms) while evidence extraction only starts after analysis (~13.5s). That separation is incidental — a slow poster decode on a large clip, or a faster analysis path, could overlap them.

Fix direction: one shared queue both modules go through. That lands naturally with strides-k03, which already proposes lifting the shared <video> primitives (seekTo, waitForPresentedFrame, waitForDecodedData, HAVE_CURRENT_DATA, the teardown) out of extractFrames.ts into a common module — the queue belongs in the same place.

Low priority: the observed peak is 1 of each, the decoders are short-lived, and the failure mode is memory pressure rather than incorrectness.
close_reason: Fixed and merged 2026-08-29 (e8ce0e9), landing with strides-k03 exactly as the bead predicted. One shared queueDetachedDecode in src/video/videoElement.ts replaces the two module-level queues, so the ceiling of one detached decoder is now global rather than per-kind. Confirmed by MUTATION, not inspection: restoring posterFrame.ts's private queue reproduces the log 'open:1 open:2 close:1 close:2' - the structural peak of 2 this bead describes - and three new tests fail; reverting turns them green. The tests are only writable in videoElement.test.ts, because each feature's own suite imports one consumer and is structurally blind to the pair, which is precisely why both suites were fully green while the defect existed. Spec handled by ADDING 'One transient video decoder across every feature that opens one' to video-input rather than MODIFYing the three requirements that assert the per-feature ceiling: none of them is falsified (a global ceiling implies each per-feature one), and what the spec actually lacked was the ceiling for the PAIR, which is a property of neither feature - as written the spec permitted re-splitting the queues and reintroducing this defect.

title: Preview stage letterboxes a portrait clip
description:
Cosmetic, observed by strides-kyu.5 and deliberately left alone.

The preview stage is a landscape max-w-5xl box, so a portrait clip (Demo 2 is 2160x3840) renders with black pillarboxing. Visible in kyu.5's own screenshot.

Fixing it means sizing the stage to the clip's aspect ratio, which needs `metadata` plumbed into ClipStripEntry — and it touches classes that are load-bearing for the strip thumbnail placement, where the video's box size is part of the on-screen-throughput guarantee (strides-kyu.13). Not worth risking that for pillarboxing.

If picked up: verify the mid-analysis playback-arm number afterwards (Demo 2, 5 trials, target ~63 median, failure band 47-49), not just that it looks right.
close_reason: Won't fix, decided 2026-08-29 on the bead's own reasoning. Sizing the preview stage to clip aspect ratio touches classes load-bearing for the on-screen-throughput guarantee (strides-kyu.13: a concealed clip costs ~20% of sampled frames on the playback arm, 63 -> 47-49). Cosmetic pillarboxing does not justify risking that, and the verification cost (5-trial Demo 2 playback-arm re-measure) exceeds the fix.

title: stepWidth's ankle calipers are near the floor of legibility
description:
Observed by strides-ac9.8 while visually reviewing every rendered thumbnail. Reported, not fixed — and it may not want fixing.

On Demo 2, stepWidth's pair caliper renders correctly: hip-width segments and both midline plumbs are clear. But the ankle offset calipers themselves are TINY, because the measured offset genuinely IS a few pixels on a front view. The mark is an honest depiction of a small quantity.

That is the tension. Enlarging it would misrepresent the measurement — exactly what this change's honesty requirement forbids. Options, none obviously right:
- leave it (the picture is truthful; a small measurement looks small)
- tighten the crop for stepWidth specifically so the same offset occupies more pixels
- add an end-tick or emphasis treatment that makes a short caliper findable without changing its length

Interacts with GitHub #71 and with EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX = 320, whose stated rationale is already stale (it was sized for 200-400 CSS px gallery images; inline thumbnails are smaller). #71 is explicit that the 320 floor must not simply be moved. Decide with a measurement, not by picking a number.
close_reason: Working as intended, decided 2026-08-29. The ankle offset on a front view genuinely IS a few pixels, and the mark is an honest depiction of a small quantity. Enlarging it would misrepresent the measurement, which the results-view honesty requirement forbids ('An annotation depicts what was measured at the depicted instant, never the card's reported value'). Neither of the two alternatives is worth its cost: a crop tightening interacts with EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX which must not move, and an emphasis treatment adds draw-layer surface for a mark that is already correct.

title: Extract shared <video> primitives out of extractFrames.ts
description:
Review finding 4 from strides-kyu.2, deferred as a follow-up rather than blocking the epic.

posterFrame.ts imports `seekTo`/`waitForPresentedFrame` from extractFrames.ts (sound — both are generic <video> primitives carrying no evidence-epic policy) but then RE-IMPLEMENTS a third, `waitForDecodedData` (posterFrame.ts:133-156), byte-for-byte identical to extractFrames.ts:252-278. Plus a duplicate HAVE_CURRENT_DATA (:59 vs extractFrames.ts:83), a duplicate timeout constant (POSTER_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS vs LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS, same 10000, near-identical doc), and a deriveClipPoster try/finally teardown duplicating extractClipEvidence's comment-for-comment.

Cost: a fix to the decoder-teardown sequence or the readiness wait must now be made twice, and only one site is reachable by grepping the other's imports.

Fix: lift the four primitives into a shared `src/video/videoElement.ts` that both import. This removes the coupling entirely rather than undoing the import.

Second reason to do it: extractFrames.ts:28 states 'Runs strictly after phase: ready, never inside the sampling loop.' useClipPoster deliberately runs its borrowed halves DURING sampling (useClipPoster.ts:20-25). That choice is argued and reasonable, but it makes the borrowed module's stated invariant false for one of its consumers.

Also fold in review finding 5 (minor): deriveClipPoster's doc claims 'every failure is a null, never a throw' (posterFrame.ts:164) but :217-230 is try/finally with no catch, and useClipPoster.ts:41 has no rejection handler. Either add the catch or correct the doc. Note EvidenceGallery.tsx:416 has the identical shape, so this is a repo-wide pattern rather than a new deviation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The four duplicated primitives live in one shared module imported by both consumers
- [ ] No behavior change; tsc -b, npm test, eslint clean
- [ ] deriveClipPoster's stated never-throws contract and its code agree
close_reason: Fixed and merged 2026-08-29 (e8ce0e9; openspec change share-one-detached-video-decoder archived). Four duplicated primitives lifted into the new src/video/videoElement.ts: waitForDecodedData (which posterFrame.ts had re-implemented byte-for-byte), HAVE_CURRENT_DATA, the timeout constants, and the decoder open/teardown sequence, plus seekTo/waitForPresentedFrame which posterFrame had merely borrowed. All 15 moved blocks proven byte-identical by mechanical string comparison against 'git show HEAD:', not by inspection. Three doc sentences deliberately RESTATED rather than transplanted because each was true only of the evidence path (the load timeout's 'already decoded once by the analysis pass', seekTo's 'must mark the metric extraction-failed', and the schedule claim). The 'runs strictly after phase: ready' contradiction resolved by leaving the invariant in extractFrames.ts and having videoElement.ts state explicitly that it carries no schedule - it is a fact about when extraction is CALLED, not a property of a seek, and useClipPoster runs the same primitives DURING sampling by design. deriveClipPoster's throw/doc mismatch fixed on the DOC side, not by adding a catch: an existing test deliberately pins it REJECTING when createObjectURL throws and pins that the queue survives, so a catch would delete an asserted behaviour inside a behaviour-preserving refactor, and would erase the only signal that a genuine bug exists. 87 files/1314 tests green, live check clean on both demos, anchor exact.

title: Aggregate multi-clip progress becomes a value with no consumer
description:
Follow-up surfaced by the navbar-clip-shell spec pass, deliberately left out of scope there.

`openspec/specs/multi-clip-analysis/spec.md` 'Aggregate multi-clip analysis state' specifies `progress` as the mean of every clip's own progress. Once per-clip progress renders on navbar thumbnails (strides-kyu.4), nothing renders the aggregate mean.

The requirement is not FALSE — `computeAggregateAnalysisState` still computes it — but it now describes a value with no consumer. The spec pass left it alone rather than modify a requirement outside its remit.

Decide: drop the field (and its spec clause), or keep it and document why. Low priority, no user-visible effect either way.
close_reason: Decision taken: keep computeAggregateAnalysisState and its spec clause. Own body records no user-visible effect either way; not worth a spec MODIFIED delta and its clobber surface.

title: Demo 1 verticalOscillationCm heads newly clipped at the top edge after crop centring
description:
Found by UX review of strides-e9b. On the Demo 1 track clip, verticalOscillationCm's ghosted pair had both heads fully in frame on main and now has them clipped at the top edge. Cosmetic — the hip cross and bounce guides are dead-centre and every mark is inside the crop.

Worth recording as the one place Demo 1 went backwards, against verticalRatio stridePair and kneeFlexion which both IMPROVED on the same clip (heads previously clipped, now fully in frame with clearance). Net effect on Demo 1 is positive; this is the exception.
notes: From the same sweep as strides-hle, strides-830 and the Demo 2 edge-bystander finding. Do not fix by moving EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX.
close_reason: Cosmetic, and describes the same absent strides-e9b crop-centring code as strides-830/hle. Not current behaviour on main.

title: Spec prose at form-heuristics:1270 loosely describes overstriding's pair after quality ranking
description:
Found in code review of strides-9mb. openspec/specs/form-heuristics/spec.md:1270 says overstriding 'pairs its furthest-reaching strike with its closest-landing one'. Since strides-9mb, each end of the range is filled by the best-SCORING surviving candidate at that end, not necessarily the furthest-reaching one — extremeness is only a tie-break. The sentence sits in the per-instant-side requirement and the point it is making (nothing constrains the two instants to one foot) is unaffected, so this is wording accuracy, not a behaviour contradiction.

Deliberately NOT folded into rank-range-exemplar-ends-by-quality: that change MODIFIES a different requirement, and widening it to a second requirement would have added clobber surface for a purely cosmetic gain.
notes: Filed because strides-9mb's design.md D6 said this was 'tracked as debt' when no bead actually covered it. Now it is tracked.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-08-29. openspec/specs/form-heuristics/spec.md now says overstriding 'pairs a far-reaching strike with a close-landing one - one drawn from each end of its range, where each end is filled by the best-scoring surviving candidate at that end and extremeness is only a tie-break'. Corrects the stale 'furthest-reaching / closest-landing' claim left by strides-9mb's ranking change, while preserving the sentence's actual point (nothing constrains the two instants to one foot). Applied as a direct spec-drift correction rather than an openspec MODIFIED block: the behaviour already shipped under strides-9mb, so there is no delta to propose, and a MODIFIED block replaces the whole requirement body - more clobber surface than a one-sentence prose fix is worth, which is the bead's own stated reasoning. openspec validate --specs --strict: 9 passed, 0 failed.

title: Valgus/pronation proxy: blocked on rear-view or dead-front-on footage
description: Spike #47 (branch spike-heel-whip-pronation) returned NO-GO on silhouette-major-axis PCA: gate 2 failed on eigenvalue identity swapping (16-25% of transitions swing >90deg, visually confirmed as noise), and gate 3 revealed a sagittal/frontal-plane confound that no noise reduction fixes. Two narrower follow-ups: (a) track mask-centroid lateral displacement instead of a fitted major axis — no 'which axis wins' instability, cheap to try on park-approach.mp4 without new footage; (b) get a true rear-view or dead-front-on clip, which unblocks the original heel-whip and heel-roll signals AND lets the centroid variant be evaluated free of the confound.
notes: Full findings in CLAUDE.md, 'Dynamic valgus proxy investigation (2026-08-14)'. Naming discipline: 'dynamic valgus proxy' only, never 'pronation'. Prospective openspec slug: dynamic-valgus-proxy-metric.

title: Slow-motion detection: blocked on a real device-native slo-mo clip
description: Spike #42 (branch spike-slowmo-detection) built containerTiming.ts + slowMotionDetection.ts and concluded detect-and-caveat, not detect-and-rescale. Not shipped.
